title.zh: 卷七十九 列傳第四 高祖諸子
title.raw: 卷七十九 列傳第四 高祖諸子 Volume 79 Biographies 4: Sons of Gaozu

sentences.zh: 高祖諸子

translations.literal: The sons of Gaozu
translations.idiomatic: The Sons of Gaozu

sentences.zh: 隱太子建成衛王玄霸巢王元吉楚王智雲荊王元景漢王元昌酆王元亨周王元方徐王元禮韓王元嘉黃公訁喿彭王元則鄭王元懿霍王元軌虢王鳳道王元慶鄧王元裕舒王元名魯王靈夔江王元祥密王元曉滕王元嬰

translations.literal: The Hidden Crown Prince Jian, Prince Wei Xuanba, Prince Chao Yuanji, Prince Chu Zhiyun, Prince Jing Yuanjing, Prince Han Yuanchang, Prince Feng Yuanheng, Prince Zhou Yuanfang, Prince Xu Yuanli, Prince Han Yuanjia, Prince Huang Yuan Shao, Prince Peng Yuanze, Prince Zheng Yuanyi, Prince Huo Yuangui, Prince Guo Feng, Prince Dao Yuanqing, Prince Deng Yuanyu, Prince Shu Yuanming, Prince Lu Lingkui, Prince Jiang Yuanxiang, Prince Mi Yuanxiao, and Prince Teng Yuanying
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Jian (posthumously styled the Hidden Crown Prince), Princes Wei Xuanba, Chao Yuanji, Chu Zhiyun, Jing Yuanjing, Han Yuanchang, Feng Yuanheng, Zhou Yuanfang, Xu Yuanli, Han Yuanjia, Huang Yuan Shao, Peng Yuanze, Zheng Yuanyi, Huo Yuangui, Guo Feng, Dao Yuanqing, Deng Yuanyu, Shu Yuanming, Lu Lingkui, Jiang Yuanxiang, Mi Yuanxiao, and Teng Yuanying

sentences.zh: 高祖二十二子：竇皇后生建成、太宗皇帝、玄霸、元吉，萬貴妃生智雲，莫嬪生元景，孫嬪生元昌，尹德妃生元亨，張氏生元方，郭婕妤生元禮，宇文昭儀生元嘉及第十九子靈夔，王才人生元則，張寶林生元懿，張美人生元軌，楊美人生鳳，劉婕妤生元慶，崔嬪生元裕，小楊嬪生元名，楊嬪生元祥，魯才人生元曉，柳寶林生元嬰。

translations.literal: Gaozu had twenty-two sons: Empress Dou bore Jian, the Emperor Taizong, Xuanba, and Yuanji; Consort Wan bore Zhiyun; Lady Mo bore Yuanjing; Lady Sun bore Yuanchang; Lady Yin bore Yuanheng; Lady Zhang bore Yuanfang; Lady Guo bore Yuanli; Lady Yuwen bore Yuanjia and the nineteenth son Lingkui; Lady Wang bore Yuanze; Lady Zhang Baolin bore Yuanyi; Lady Zhang Mei bore Yuangui; Lady Yang bore Feng; Lady Liu bore Yuanqing; Lady Cui bore Yuanyu; the Lesser Lady Yang bore Yuanming; Lady Yang bore Yuanxiang; Lady Lu bore Yuanxiao; and Lady Liu Baolin bore Yuanying.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu had twenty-two sons. Empress Dou gave birth to Jian, the future Emperor Taizong, Xuanba, and Yuanji. Consort Wan bore Zhiyun; Lady Mo, Yuanjing; Lady Sun, Yuanchang; Lady Yin, Yuanheng; Lady Zhang, Yuanfang; Lady Guo, Yuanli; Lady Yuwen, Yuanjia and the nineteenth son, Lingkui; Lady Wang, Yuanze; Lady Zhang Baolin, Yuanyi; Lady Zhang Mei, Yuangui; Lady Yang, Feng; Lady Liu, Yuanqing; Lady Cui, Yuanyu; the lesser Lady Yang, Yuanming; another Lady Yang, Yuanxiang; Lady Lu, Yuanxiao; and Lady Liu Baolin, Yuanying.

sentences.zh: 隱太子建成小字毘沙門。

translations.literal: The Hidden Crown Prince Jian had the childhood name Vaisravana.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Jian, later styled the Hidden Crown Prince, was called by the childhood name Vaisravana.

sentences.zh: 資簡弛，不治常檢，荒色嗜酒，畋獵無度，所從皆博徒大俠。

translations.literal: His nature was lax and undisciplined; he did not keep to ordinary rules, indulged in lust and wine, hunted without limit, and those who followed him were all gamblers and roaming bravos.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was easygoing and careless of propriety, heedless of routine discipline, given to dissipation and drink, and to hunting without restraint; his companions were gamblers and swaggering swordsmen.

sentences.zh: 隋末，高祖被詔捕賊汾、晉間，留建成護家，居河東。

translations.literal: At the end of the Sui, Gaozu was ordered by edict to capture bandits between Fen and Jin, and left Jian to guard the household, residing in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Sui, when Gaozu was ordered to hunt down bandits in the Fen and Jin region, he left Jian at home to look after the family in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 高祖已起兵，密召與元吉赴太原，隋人購之急，從間道至，授左領軍大都督，封隴西郡公。

translations.literal: After Gaozu had raised troops, he secretly summoned him and Yuanji to Taiyuan; the Sui sought them urgently, but they came by a hidden route and were appointed Left Commander-in-Chief of the Army and enfeoffed as Duke of Longxi commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Once Gaozu had risen in arms, he secretly called Jian and Yuanji to Taiyuan. The Sui court put a price on their heads, but they reached him by back roads; he made Jian Left Commander-in-Chief of the Army and enfeoffed him as Duke of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 引兵略定西河，從平京師。

translations.literal: He led troops to seize and pacify Xihe and followed in the pacification of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He led forces to subdue Xihe and took part in the capture of the capital.

sentences.zh: 唐國建，為世子，開府置官屬。

translations.literal: When the state of Tang was established, he was made heir apparent, opened a princely establishment, and appointed officials.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tang state was founded, he was named heir apparent, established his own princely staff, and appointed a full household of officials.

sentences.zh: 又遷撫軍大將軍，為東討元帥，將萬人徇洛陽，授尚書令。

translations.literal: He was further promoted to General Who Pacifies the Army, made marshal of the eastern campaign, led ten thousand men against Luoyang, and was appointed Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made General Who Pacifies the Army and marshal of the eastern expedition, led ten thousand troops toward Luoyang, and was appointed Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，立為皇太子。

translations.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication, Jian was installed as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozu took the throne, Jian was installed as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 詔率將軍桑顯和擊司竹群盜，平之。

translations.literal: By edict he led General Sang Xianhe to attack the bandit gangs of Sizhu and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered him to lead General Sang Xianhe against the bandit gangs of Sizhu, and they were put down.

sentences.zh: 涼州人安興貴殺李軌，以眾降，詔趣原州應接。

translations.literal: An Xinggui of Liangzhou killed Li Gui and surrendered with his followers; an edict urged him to hurry from Yuanzhou to receive them.
translations.idiomatic: An Xinggui of Liangzhou killed Li Gui and came over with his troops; Jian was ordered to hurry from Yuanzhou to meet and accept the surrender.

sentences.zh: 建成素驕，不恤士，雖甚署，晝夜馳獵，眾不堪其勞，亡者過半。

translations.literal: Jian had always been arrogant and did not care for the troops; though he pressed them hard, he hunted day and night, the men could not bear the labor, and more than half fled.
translations.idiomatic: Jian had long been arrogant and indifferent to his soldiers. Though he drove them hard, he hunted day and night; the men could not endure the strain, and more than half deserted.

sentences.zh: 帝欲其習事，乃敕非軍國大務聽裁決之。

translations.literal: The emperor wished him to gain practice in affairs, and therefore ordered that he might decide all matters that were not great affairs of state and army.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wanted him to learn how to govern, and decreed that he might decide any matter that was not a major military or state affair.

sentences.zh: 又以李綱、鄭善果為宮官，參謀議。

translations.literal: He also appointed Li Gang and Zheng Shanguo as palace officials to take part in deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: He also appointed Li Gang and Zheng Shanguo as palace advisers to counsel the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 稽胡劉屳成寇邊，詔建成進討，破之鄠州，斬虜千計，引渠長悉官之，使還招群胡。

translations.literal: The Ji Hu leader Liu Xincheng raided the border; an edict ordered Jian to advance against him; he defeated him at Ezhou, beheaded enemies by the thousands, brought all the channel chiefs into office, and sent them back to summon the Hu clans.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ji Hu chieftain Liu Xincheng raided the frontier, Jian was ordered to campaign against him. He routed him at Ezhou, killed thousands of the enemy, appointed all the local chiefs to office, and sent them back to win over the other Hu groups.

sentences.zh: 屳成與它大帥降，建成畏其眾，紿欲城州縣者，使降胡操築，陰勒兵殺六千人，屳成奔梁師都。

translations.literal: Xincheng and other great chiefs surrendered; Jian feared their numbers, deceived those who wished to fortify prefectures and counties, made the surrendered Hu work on construction, secretly urged troops to kill six thousand of them, and Xincheng fled to Liang Shidu.
translations.idiomatic: Xincheng and other major chiefs submitted, but Jian feared their numbers. He tricked those who wanted to garrison the prefectures and counties into having the surrendered Hu labor on fortifications, then secretly ordered his troops to slaughter six thousand of them; Xincheng fled to Liang Shidu.

sentences.zh: 嘗循行北邊，遇賊四百出降，悉馘其耳縱之。

translations.literal: Once on patrol along the northern border he met four hundred bandits coming out to surrender; he cut off all their ears and released them.
translations.idiomatic: Once while patrolling the northern frontier he met four hundred bandits who came out to surrender; he had all their ears cut off and then let them go.

sentences.zh: 中允王珪、洗馬魏征以帝初興，建成不知謀，而秦王數平劇寇，功冠天下，英豪歸之，陰許立為皇太子，勢危甚。

translations.literal: The Palace Companion Wang Gui and the Stud Groom Wei Zheng, because the empire was newly risen and Jian did not know strategy while the Prince of Qin repeatedly pacified fierce bandits and his merit topped the realm so that heroes turned to him, secretly promised to make him crown prince; the situation was very perilous.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Companion Wang Gui and the Stud Groom Wei Zheng saw that with the dynasty newly founded, Jian lacked strategic talent while the Prince of Qin had repeatedly crushed formidable rebels, his achievements unmatched and men of talent flocking to him. They secretly promised to secure the crown princehood for him, and Jian's position grew precarious.

sentences.zh: 會劉黑闥亂河北，珪等進說曰：「殿下特以嫡長居東宮，非有功德為人所稱道。

translations.literal: When Liu Heita rebelled in Hebei, Gui and the others advanced and said: 'Your Highness sits in the Eastern Palace only because you are the eldest legitimate son; you have no merit that men praise.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Heita rose in Hebei, Wang Gui and his colleagues urged him: 'Your Highness holds the Eastern Palace only as eldest legitimate son—you have no achievements that win men's praise.

sentences.zh: 今黑闥痍叛殘孽，眾不盈萬，利兵鏖之，唾手可決，請往討，因結山東英俊心，自封殖。」

translations.literal: Now Heita is a wounded rebel remnant, his followers not yet ten thousand; with sharp troops grinding him down, the matter can be settled at a breath—please go to campaign, thereby binding the hearts of the talented men of the east and building your own foundation.'
translations.idiomatic: Heita is only a crippled remnant of rebellion, with fewer than ten thousand men. Send a strong force against him and the affair is settled in a trice. Go yourself to suppress him, win over the outstanding men of the east, and build your own power base.'

sentences.zh: 建成遂請行。

translations.literal: Jian thereupon requested to go.
translations.idiomatic: Jian then asked to lead the campaign himself.

sentences.zh: 黑闥敗洺水，建成問征曰：「山東其定乎？」

translations.literal: Heita was defeated at the Ming River; Jian asked Wei Zheng: 'Will the east be settled?'
translations.idiomatic: After Heita was defeated at the Ming River, Jian asked Wei Zheng, 'Will the east now be pacified?'

sentences.zh: 對曰：「黑闥雖敗，殺傷太甚，其魁黨皆縣名處死，妻子系虜，欲降無繇，雖有赦令，獲者必戮，不大蕩宥，恐殘賊嘯結，民未可安。」

translations.literal: He replied: 'Though Heita is defeated, the killing and wounding were too severe; his chiefs and partisans were all sentenced to death by name, wives and children bound as captives—those who wished to surrender had no means. Though there was an amnesty edict, any who were caught were certainly executed. Without a broad sweeping pardon, I fear the remnant bandits will gather and howl together, and the people cannot yet be at peace.'
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng answered: 'Heita may be beaten, but the slaughter was too great. His leaders were all marked for execution by name, their families taken captive—those who wanted to submit had no way to do so. Even when an amnesty was proclaimed, anyone captured was still put to death. Unless you grant a sweeping pardon, the surviving rebels will rally again and the people will never be secure.'

sentences.zh: 既而黑闥復振，廬江王瑗棄洺州，山東亂。

translations.literal: Before long Heita revived; the Prince of Lujiang Yuan abandoned Mingzhou, and the east was in turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Heita rallied again; Prince Lujiang Yuan abandoned Mingzhou, and the east erupted once more.

sentences.zh: 命齊王元吉討之，有詔降者赦罪，眾不信。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qi Yuanji was ordered to campaign against him; an edict promised amnesty to those who surrendered, but the masses did not believe it.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qi, Yuanji, was sent to suppress him. An edict promised pardon to anyone who surrendered, but no one believed it.

sentences.zh: 建成至，獲俘皆撫遣之，百姓欣悅。

translations.literal: When Jian arrived, all captives taken were comforted and sent away, and the common people were delighted.
translations.idiomatic: When Jian arrived, he treated every captive with kindness and released them, to the great joy of the people.

sentences.zh: 賊懼，夜奔，兵追戰。

translations.literal: The rebels were afraid, fled by night, and the troops pursued and fought.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels panicked and fled by night; Jian's troops pursued and gave battle.

sentences.zh: 黑闥眾猶盛，乃縱囚使相告曰：「褫而甲還鄉里，若妻子獲者，既已釋矣。」

translations.literal: Heita's forces were still strong; Jian then released prisoners and had them tell one another: 'Strip off your armor and return to your villages; if your wives and children were taken, they have already been released.'
translations.idiomatic: Heita's army was still formidable, so Jian released prisoners to spread the word: 'Lay down your arms and go home—if your families were captured, they have already been freed.'

sentences.zh: 眾乃散，或縛其渠長降，遂禽黑闥。

translations.literal: The masses then dispersed; some bound their chiefs and surrendered, and Heita was finally captured.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels scattered; some tied up their leaders and submitted, and Heita was captured at last.

sentences.zh: 帝晚多內寵，張婕妤、尹德妃最幸，親戚分事宮府。

translations.literal: In his later years the emperor had many inner favorites; Lady Zhang and Lady Yin were most favored, and their kin took charge of affairs in palace and princely establishments.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years the emperor favored many consorts; Lady Zhang and Lady Yin enjoyed his special affection, and their relatives took up posts throughout the palace and the princely households.

sentences.zh: 建成與元吉通謀，內結妃禦以自固。

translations.literal: Jian and Yuanji conspired together and won over the inner consorts to strengthen themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Jian and Yuanji plotted together and cultivated alliances with the emperor's favored consorts to shore up their position.

sentences.zh: 當是時，海內未定，秦王數將兵在外，諸妃希所見。

translations.literal: At that time the realm was not yet settled; the Prince of Qin repeatedly led troops abroad, and the various consorts rarely saw him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the empire was still unsettled; the Prince of Qin was often away on campaign, and the consorts seldom saw him.

sentences.zh: 及洛陽平，帝遣諸妃馳閱後宮，見府庫服玩，皆私有求索，為兄弟請官。

translations.literal: When Luoyang was pacified, the emperor sent the consorts in haste to inspect the rear palaces; seeing the storehouses of robes and curios, they all sought them for private possession and asked offices for their brothers.
translations.idiomatic: After Luoyang fell, the emperor sent his consorts to tour the palaces there. Seeing the treasuries of robes and luxuries, they claimed what they wanted for themselves and pressed for offices for their brothers.

sentences.zh: 秦王已封帑簿，及官爵非有功不得，妃媛曹怨之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin had sealed the treasury registers, and offices and ranks could not be obtained without merit; the consorts and their cliques resented him.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qin had sealed the treasury ledgers and insisted that offices and titles go only to men of merit; the consorts and their factions bore him a grudge.

sentences.zh: 會為陜東道行臺，有詔屬內得專處決。

translations.literal: He was at the time made Eastern-Shaanxi Circuit Commissioner, and an edict allowed him to decide matters within his jurisdiction on his own authority.
translations.idiomatic: When he became commissioner of the Eastern Shaanxi circuit, an edict empowered him to decide all matters within his jurisdiction on his own authority.

sentences.zh: 王以美田給淮安王神通，而張婕妤為父丐之，帝手詔賜田，詔至，神通已得前，不肯與。

translations.literal: The prince gave fine fields to the Prince of Huai'an Li Shentong, but Lady Zhang begged them for her father; the emperor personally wrote an edict granting the fields, but when the edict arrived Shentong had already received them beforehand and would not yield them.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qin had assigned fine fields to Prince Huai'an Li Shentong, but Lady Zhang pleaded for them on her father's behalf. The emperor wrote a personal edict granting the land, yet by the time it arrived Shentong had already taken possession and refused to give them up.

sentences.zh: 婕妤妄曰：「詔賜妾父田，而王奪與人。」

translations.literal: The lady falsely said: 'The edict granted fields to my father, yet the prince seized them and gave them to another.'
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zhang falsely claimed, 'The edict gave the fields to my father, yet the prince stole them and handed them to someone else.'

sentences.zh: 帝怒，召秦王讓曰：「我詔令不如爾教邪？」

translations.literal: The emperor was angry, summoned the Prince of Qin, and reproached him: 'Are my edicts inferior to your instructions?'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage, summoned the Prince of Qin, and rebuked him: 'Do my edicts count for less than your orders?'

sentences.zh: 他日，謂裴寂曰：「兒久典兵，為儒生所誤，非復我昔日子。」

translations.literal: Another day he said to Pei Ji: 'The boy has long commanded troops and is misled by Confucian scholars; he is no longer the son I once knew.'
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion he told Pei Ji, 'That boy has commanded armies too long and lets the pedants lead him astray—he is not the son I used to know.'

sentences.zh: 秦府屬杜如晦騎過尹妃父門，恚其傲，率家童捽毆，折一指。

translations.literal: Du Ruhui of the Qin establishment rode past the gate of Lady Yin's father, resented his arrogance, led household boys to seize and beat him, and broke one finger.
translations.idiomatic: Du Ruhui of the Prince of Qin's staff rode past the home of Lady Yin's father, took offense at his insolence, and with household servants seized and beat him, breaking a finger.

sentences.zh: 父懼，即使妃前訴秦王左右暴其父，帝不察，大怒，詰王曰：「兒左右乃淩我妃家，況百姓乎？」

translations.literal: ' The father was afraid and at once had the consort go before the throne to complain that the prince's attendants had abused her father; the emperor did not investigate, was greatly angry, and interrogated the prince: 'Your attendants bully my consort's family—what of the common people?'
translations.idiomatic: ' Terrified, the father sent his daughter to accuse the prince's men of assaulting him. The emperor did not look into the matter, flew into a rage, and demanded of the prince, 'If your followers bully my consort's kin, what must they do to ordinary people?'

sentences.zh: 王自辨曉，訖不置，繇是見疏。

translations.literal: The prince explained himself until dawn, but in the end nothing was done; from this he came to be estranged.
translations.idiomatic: The prince pleaded his case until dawn, yet the matter was never resolved; from then on the emperor grew distant toward him.

sentences.zh: 帝召諸王燕，秦王感母之不及有天下也，偶獨泣，帝顧不樂，妃媛因得中傷之，為建成遊說曰：「海內無事，陛下春秋高，當自娛，秦王輒悲泣，正為嗔忌妾屬耳。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned the princes to a banquet; the Prince of Qin, moved that his mother did not live to see the possession of the realm, wept alone by chance; the emperor looked and was displeased; the consorts thereby gained occasion to slander him and pleaded Jian's cause, saying: 'Within the seas there is no trouble; Your Majesty's years are advanced and you should enjoy yourself—yet the Prince of Qin constantly weeps in grief, which is plainly resentment and jealousy toward us consorts.
translations.idiomatic: At a banquet for the princes, the Prince of Qin, thinking of how his mother never lived to see the empire won, wept quietly by himself. The emperor's face darkened. The consorts seized the chance to slander him to Jian's advantage: 'The realm is at peace and Your Majesty should enjoy your years, yet the Prince of Qin keeps weeping—clearly he resents us.

sentences.zh: 使陛下萬歲後，王得誌，妾屬無遺類。

translations.literal: If after Your Majesty's ten thousand years the prince attains his will, we consorts will not leave a single survivor.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty is gone and he has his way, not one of us will be left alive.

sentences.zh: 東宮慈愛，必能全養。」

translations.literal: The Eastern Palace is kindly and loving and will surely preserve and nurture us all.'
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Palace is gentle and kind—he will surely protect us.'

sentences.zh: 乃皆悲不自勝。

translations.literal: They all then grieved beyond control.
translations.idiomatic: They all broke down in tears.

sentences.zh: 帝惻然，遂無易太子意。

translations.literal: The emperor was moved to pity and thereafter had no thought of changing the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Moved to pity, the emperor abandoned any thought of replacing the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 突厥入寇，帝議遷都，秦王苦諫止。

translations.literal: The Turks invaded; the emperor discussed moving the capital; the Prince of Qin remonstrated bitterly and stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: When the Turks raided the frontier, the emperor considered moving the capital; the Prince of Qin argued strenuously against it and prevailed.

sentences.zh: 建成見帝曰：「秦王欲外禦寇，沮遷都議，以久其兵，而謀篡奪。」

translations.literal: Jian saw the emperor and said: 'The Prince of Qin wishes to defend against invaders abroad, obstructed the plan to move the capital in order to prolong his command of troops, and plots usurpation.'
translations.idiomatic: Jian told the emperor, 'The Prince of Qin only wants to keep his army in the field by blocking the move of the capital so he can defend against the Turks abroad—he is plotting a coup.'

sentences.zh: 帝浸不悅。

translations.literal: The emperor gradually became displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's displeasure with the prince deepened.

sentences.zh: 初，帝令秦王居西宮承乾殿，元吉居武德殿，與上臺、東宮晝夜往來，皆攜弓刀，相遇如家人禮。

translations.literal: At first the emperor ordered the Prince of Qin to reside in the Chengqian Hall of the Western Palace and Yuanji in the Wude Hall; they came and went day and night with the emperor's terrace and the Eastern Palace, all carrying bow and blade, meeting one another with the etiquette of family kin.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the emperor had the Prince of Qin live in the Chengqian Hall of the Western Palace and Yuanji in the Wude Hall. They passed back and forth day and night between the imperial quarters, the Eastern Palace, and one another, always armed with bow and sword, greeting each other like members of one household.

sentences.zh: 由是皇太子令、秦齊二王教與詔敕雜行，內外懼，莫知所從。

translations.literal: From this the crown prince's orders, the instructions of the Princes of Qin and Qi, and imperial edicts were issued mixed together; inside and outside were afraid and did not know whom to follow.
translations.idiomatic: As a result, orders from the crown prince, directives from the Princes of Qin and Qi, and imperial edicts all circulated at once; court and capital alike were alarmed, unsure whose word to obey.

sentences.zh: 建成等私募四方驍勇及長安惡少年二千人為宮甲，屯左右長林門，號「長林兵」。

translations.literal: Jian and the others secretly recruited two thousand fierce warriors from the four quarters and vicious youths of Chang'an as palace guards, stationed them at the left and right Changlin Gates, and called them the 'Changlin troops.'
translations.idiomatic: Jian and his party secretly enlisted two thousand bold fighters from across the realm and rowdy youths of Chang'an as palace guards, billeted them at the Changlin Gates, and called them the 'Changlin Corps.'

sentences.zh: 又令左虞候率可達誌募幽州突厥兵三百內宮中，將攻西宮。

translations.literal: He also ordered the Left Palace Guard Commander Kedazhi to recruit three hundred Turk troops of Youzhou into the inner palace, intending to attack the Western Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He further ordered the Left Palace Guard commander Kedazhi to bring three hundred Youzhou Turk soldiers into the inner palace, planning an assault on the Western Palace.

sentences.zh: 或告於帝，帝召建成責謂，乃流誌巂州。

translations.literal: Someone reported to the emperor; the emperor summoned Jian and reproached him, and then exiled Zhi to Xizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the emperor, he summoned Jian and rebuked him, then banished Kedazhi to Xizhou.

sentences.zh: 華陰楊文幹素兇诐，建成昵之，使為慶州總管，遣募兵送京師，欲為變。

translations.literal: Yang Wengan of Huayin was by nature fierce and treacherous; Jian was intimate with him, made him prefectural commander of Qingzhou, and sent him to recruit troops and convey them to the capital, intending rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Wengan of Huayin was notoriously brutal and deceitful. Jian favored him, appointed him military governor of Qingzhou, and had him raise troops for dispatch to the capital, planning a coup.

sentences.zh: 時帝幸仁智宮，秦王、元吉從，建成謂元吉曰：「秦王且遍見諸妃，彼金寶多，有以賂遺之也。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor was visiting Renzhi Palace; the Prince of Qin and Yuanji followed; Jian said to Yuanji: 'The Prince of Qin is about to visit all the consorts in turn; they have much gold and treasure, and he will bribe them with gifts.
translations.idiomatic: While the emperor was at Renzhi Palace with the Prince of Qin and Yuanji in attendance, Jian told Yuanji, 'The prince of Qin is going to pay court to every consort in turn. They have rich stores of gold and jewels—he will buy them off with gifts.

sentences.zh: 吾安得箕踞受禍？

translations.literal: How can I sit sprawled and receive disaster?
translations.idiomatic: How can I sit idle and let disaster fall on us?

sentences.zh: 安危之計決今日。」

translations.literal: The plan for safety or peril must be settled today.'
translations.idiomatic: Our fate must be decided today.'

sentences.zh: 元吉曰：「善。」

translations.literal: Yuanji said: 'Good.'
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji said, 'Agreed.'

sentences.zh: 乃命郎將尒硃煥、校尉橋公山賫甲遺文幹，趣興兵。

translations.literal: He then ordered the commandant Erzhu Huan and the captain Qiao Gongshan to carry armor to Wengan and urge him to raise troops.
translations.idiomatic: He sent the commandant Erzhu Huan and Captain Qiao Gongshan with armor to Yang Wengan, urging him to rise in arms.

sentences.zh: 煥等懼，至豳鄉白反狀，寧州人杜鳳亦上變。

translations.literal: Huan and the others were afraid; reaching Binxian they reported the rebellion; Du Feng of Ningzhou also submitted an urgent memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Huan and his party reported the plot when they reached Binxian, and Du Feng of Ningzhou also sent an emergency memorial.

sentences.zh: 帝遣司農卿宇文穎驛召文幹，元吉陰結穎，使告文幹，文幹遽率兵反。

translations.literal: The emperor sent the Minister of Agriculture Yuwen Ying by post to summon Wengan; Yuanji secretly won Ying over and had him inform Wengan, and Wengan immediately led troops in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dispatched Minister of Agriculture Yuwen Ying by fast courier to recall Wengan. Yuanji secretly won Ying over and tipped Wengan off; Wengan at once rose in revolt.

sentences.zh: 帝以建成首謀，未忍治，即詔捕王珪、魏征及左衛率韋挺、舍人徐師〓、左衛車騎馮世立，欲殺之以薄太子罪。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Jian was the chief plotter, could not bear to punish him and at once ordered the arrest of Wang Gui, Wei Zheng, the Left Guard Commander Wei Ting, the Attendant Xu Shiyuan, and the Left Guard Cavalry Officer Feng Shili, intending to kill them to lighten the crown prince's guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Jian was the mastermind, the emperor could not bring himself to punish his son. Instead he ordered Wang Gui, Wei Zheng, Left Guard commander Wei Ting, attendant Xu Shiyuan, and Left Guard cavalry officer Feng Shili arrested, planning to execute them to mitigate the crown prince's guilt.

sentences.zh: 乃手詔召建成，建成懼，不敢往。

translations.literal: He then wrote a personal edict summoning Jian; Jian was afraid and did not dare go.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote a personal summons for Jian, but Jian was too afraid to go.

sentences.zh: 師〓勸遂舉兵，詹事主簿趙弘智諫建成捐車服，輕往謝罪。

translations.literal: Shiyuan urged him to raise troops at once; the Chief Clerk of the Household Bureau Zhao Hongzhi remonstrated with Jian to cast aside carriage and robes and go lightly to beg pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shiyuan urged him to take up arms immediately, but Zhao Hongzhi, chief clerk of the crown prince's household, advised Jian to go without pomp, on foot, and throw himself on the emperor's mercy.

sentences.zh: 乃詣行在所，未至，屏官屬，徑入謁，叩頭請死，投身於地，不能起。

translations.literal: He then went to the traveling palace; before arriving he dismissed his officials, entered directly to audience, knocked his head and begged for death, threw himself on the ground, and could not rise.
translations.idiomatic: He went to the emperor's camp. Before he arrived he dismissed his attendants, entered alone, kowtowed and begged for death, then collapsed on the floor and could not rise.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，夜囚幕中，使兵衛守。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry, imprisoned him in a tent by night, and set soldiers to guard him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious. That night he had Jian confined in a tent under armed guard.

sentences.zh: 會文幹陷寧州，帝驚，以宮近賊，夜率衛士南趣，山行十餘里，明乃還宮。

translations.literal: When Wengan took Ningzhou the emperor was alarmed; because the palace was near the rebels, he led guards south by night, traveled more than ten li through the mountains, and at dawn returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Wengan seized Ningzhou, the emperor panicked. Thinking the palace too close to the rebels, he fled south by night with his guards, marching more than ten li through the hills before returning at dawn.

sentences.zh: 召秦王問計，對曰：「文幹豎子耳，官司當即禽之，就使假刻漏之久，正須遣一將可辦。」

translations.literal: He summoned the Prince of Qin to ask his plan; he replied: 'Wengan is a mere stripling; the officials will capture him at once—even granting him the longest delay of the clepsydra, one general sent is enough to settle it.'
translations.idiomatic: He called in the Prince of Qin for counsel. The prince answered, 'Wengan is a nobody—the authorities will seize him at once. Even if he gained every hour the water clock allows, one general is all you need.'

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「事連建成，恐應者眾。

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'The affair touches Jian; I fear many will respond.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, 'This involves Jian—I fear many will rally to him.

sentences.zh: 爾自行，還，吾以爾為太子，使建成王蜀，蜀地狹，不足為變，若不能事汝，取之易也。」

translations.literal: You go yourself; when you return I will make you crown prince, send Jian as king of Shu—Shu is narrow and cannot sustain a revolt—and if he will not serve you, taking it from him is easy.'
translations.idiomatic: Go yourself. When you return I will make you crown prince and send Jian to rule Shu. Shu is cramped ground—it cannot sustain a rebellion. If he will not bow to you, displacing him will be easy.'

sentences.zh: 秦王率眾趣寧州，文幹為其下所殺，以其首降，執宇文穎送京師。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin led the host toward Ningzhou; Wengan was killed by his subordinates, who surrendered with his head; Yuwen Ying was seized and sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qin marched on Ningzhou. Wengan's own men killed him and surrendered his head. Yuwen Ying was captured and sent to the capital.

sentences.zh: 秦王之行，元吉及內嬖更為建成請，封德彜亦陰說帝，由是意解，復詔建成居守，但責兄弟不相容，而謫王珪、韋挺、天策兵曹參軍杜淹於遠方。

translations.literal: ' While the Prince of Qin was on the march, Yuanji and the inner favorites again pleaded for Jian; Feng Deyi also secretly persuaded the emperor, and thereby his mind eased; he again ordered Jian to remain in charge, only reproaching the brothers for not tolerating one another, and banished Wang Gui, Wei Ting, and the Heavenly Strategies Army Registrar Du Yan to distant places.
translations.idiomatic: ' While the prince was away, Yuanji and the palace women again interceded for Jian, and Feng Deyi quietly swayed the emperor. His anger cooled; he restored Jian to his duties, rebuked the brothers only for their mutual hatred, and exiled Wang Gui, Wei Ting, and Heavenly Strategies registrar Du Yan.

sentences.zh: 然怨猜日結。

translations.literal: Yet resentment and suspicion daily tightened.
translations.idiomatic: Yet mutual resentment and suspicion only grew day by day.

sentences.zh: 建成等召秦王夜宴，毒酒而進之，王暴疾，〓血數升，淮安王扶掖還宮。

translations.literal: Jian and the others summoned the Prince of Qin to a night banquet, advanced poisoned wine, the prince fell suddenly ill and vomited several pints of blood; the Prince of Huai'an supported him back to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Jian and his party invited the Prince of Qin to a night feast and served him poisoned wine. He fell violently ill and vomited several pints of blood; Prince Huai'an helped him back to his quarters.

sentences.zh: 帝問疾，因敕建成：「秦王不能酒，毋夜聚。」

translations.literal: The emperor inquired after his illness and thereby charged Jian: 'The Prince of Qin cannot bear wine—do not gather at night.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor visited him and admonished Jian: 'The prince of Qin cannot hold his wine—no more night revels.'

sentences.zh: 又謂秦王曰：「吾起晉陽，平天下，皆爾力，將定東宮，爾亟讓，故成而美誌。

translations.literal: He also told the Prince of Qin: 'I rose from Jinyang and pacified the realm—all by your strength. I was about to fix the Eastern Palace; you urgently declined, and so it was accomplished and the record is fair.
translations.idiomatic: He also told the prince, 'I raised arms at Jinyang and won the empire through your efforts. I meant to name you heir, but you insisted on yielding—that is how matters stand, and the record honors you for it.

sentences.zh: 又太子立多歷年，吾重奪之。

translations.literal: Moreover the crown prince has stood many years; I shrink from taking it from him again.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the crown prince has held his place for many years—I cannot bear to displace him again.

sentences.zh: 觀而兄弟終不相下，同在京師，忿鬩且深。

translations.literal: Seeing that you brothers will never yield to one another, dwelling together in the capital, your anger and strife grow ever deeper.
translations.idiomatic: I see you brothers will never yield to each other. Living together in the capital, your feud only deepens.

sentences.zh: 爾還洛陽行臺，自陜以東悉主之，建天子旌旗，如梁孝王故事。」

translations.literal: Return to the Luoyang administrative commission; east of Shan commandery you shall rule all, raise the imperial banners, following the precedent of the Filial King of Liang.'
translations.idiomatic: Go back to your commission at Luoyang and rule everything east of Shan—raise the imperial banners, as the Filial King of Liang once did.'

sentences.zh: 王泣曰：「非所願也，不可遠膝下。」

translations.literal: The prince wept and said: 'It is not what I wish; I cannot be far from your knee.'
translations.idiomatic: The prince wept, 'That is not what I want—I cannot bear to leave your side.'

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「陸賈，漢臣也，猶遞過諸子，況我天下主，東西兩宮，思汝即往，何所悲邪？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'Lu Jia was a Han minister, yet he still went back and forth among the princes—how much more I, lord of the realm! With eastern and western palaces, when I think of you I can go at once—what is there to grieve?'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, 'Lu Jia was only a Han minister, yet he traveled between the princes. I am emperor—east and west palaces are not so far. When I miss you I can visit at once. Why grieve?'

sentences.zh: 王將行，建成等謀曰：「秦王得土地甲兵，必為患；

translations.literal: As the prince was about to depart, Jian and the others plotted: 'If the Prince of Qin gains territory and armor and troops, he will surely become a threat;
translations.idiomatic: As the prince prepared to leave, Jian and his allies plotted: 'If he holds territory and an army, he will become a menace;

sentences.zh: 留之京師，一匹夫耳。」

translations.literal: keep him in the capital and he is but a common man.'
translations.idiomatic: keep him in the capital and he is only a private citizen.'

sentences.zh: 因密使人說帝，言「秦王左右皆山東人，聞還洛，皆灑然喜，觀其意，不復來矣」。

translations.literal: They therefore secretly sent men to persuade the emperor, saying: 'The prince's attendants are all men of the east; hearing he is to return to Luoyang, they are all openly delighted—judging their intent, he will not come back.'
translations.idiomatic: They secretly told the emperor, 'His staff are all easterners. When they heard he was going back to Luoyang they rejoiced openly—clearly he does not mean to return.'

sentences.zh: 事果寢。

translations.literal: The affair was indeed dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 俄而突厥寇邊，太子薦元吉北討，欲因其兵作亂。

translations.literal: Before long the Turks raided the border; the crown prince recommended Yuanji for a northern campaign, intending to use his troops to make trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Turks raided the frontier. The crown prince urged sending Yuanji north, planning to use his army to stage a revolt.

sentences.zh: 長孫無忌、房玄齡、杜如晦、尉遲敬德、侯君集等勸秦王先圖之。

translations.literal: Zhangsun Wuji, Fang Xuanling, Du Ruhui, Yuchi Jingde, Hou Junji, and others urged the Prince of Qin to strike first.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Wuji, Fang Xuanling, Du Ruhui, Yuchi Jingde, Hou Junji, and others urged the prince to move against them first.

sentences.zh: 王乃密奏建成等與後宮亂，因曰：「臣無負兄弟，今乃欲殺臣，是為世充、建德復仇。

translations.literal: The prince then secretly memorialized that Jian and the others were in disorder with the inner palace, adding: 'Your servant has not failed his brothers, yet now they wish to kill me—this is to avenge Wang Shichong and Dou Jiande.
translations.idiomatic: The prince secretly reported that Jian and his party were carrying on with women of the inner palace, and added, 'I have done my brothers no wrong, yet they now seek my life—this would be vengeance for Wang Shichong and Dou Jiande.

sentences.zh: 使臣死，雖地下，愧見諸賊。」

translations.literal: If your servant dies, even beneath the earth he will be ashamed to face those rebels.'
translations.idiomatic: If I must die, I will be ashamed to face those dead rebels even in the underworld.'

sentences.zh: 帝大驚，報曰：「旦日當窮治，而必早參。」

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly alarmed and replied: 'Tomorrow we shall investigate thoroughly—you must attend court early.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was stunned and answered, 'Tomorrow I will investigate to the end—you must come to court early.'

sentences.zh: 張婕妤馳語建成，乃召元吉謀，曰：「請勒宮甲，托疾不朝。」

translations.literal: Lady Zhang galloped word to Jian; he then summoned Yuanji to plot and said: 'Please muster the palace guards and plead illness to avoid court.'
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zhang sent word in haste to Jian. He called Yuanji to counsel and said, 'Mobilize the palace guards and stay away from court on a plea of illness.'

sentences.zh: 建成曰：「善，然不共入朝，事何繇知？」

translations.literal: Jian said: 'Good—but if we do not enter court together, how shall we know how matters stand?'
translations.idiomatic: Jian said, 'Good—but if we do not go to court together, how will we learn what is happening?'

sentences.zh: 遲明，乘馬至玄武門，秦王先至，以勇士九人自衛。

translations.literal: At the late dawn they rode to the Xuanwu Gate; the Prince of Qin had arrived first with nine brave warriors to guard himself.
translations.idiomatic: At first light they rode to the Xuanwu Gate. The prince of Qin was already there, with nine stalwart warriors as his guard.

sentences.zh: 時帝已召裴寂、蕭瑀、陳叔達、封德彜、宇文士及、竇誕、顏師古等入。

translations.literal: By then the emperor had already summoned Pei Ji, Xiao Yu, Chen Shuda, Feng Deyi, Yuwen Shiji, Dou Dan, Yan Shigu, and others to enter.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had already summoned Pei Ji, Xiao Yu, Chen Shuda, Feng Deyi, Yuwen Shiji, Dou Dan, Yan Shigu, and the rest.

sentences.zh: 建成、元吉至臨湖殿，覺變，遽反走，秦王隨呼之，元吉引弓欲射，不能彀者三。

translations.literal: Jian and Yuanji reached the Linhu Hall, sensed the change, turned and fled at once; the Prince of Qin called after them; Yuanji drew his bow intending to shoot but could not fully draw it three times.
translations.idiomatic: Jian and Yuanji reached the Linhu Hall, sensed trouble, and wheeled to flee. The prince called after them. Yuanji drew his bow to shoot but three times could not fully draw it.

sentences.zh: 秦王射建成即死，元吉中矢走，敬德追殺之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin shot Jian and he died at once; Yuanji was struck by an arrow and fled; Jingde pursued and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: The prince shot Jian dead on the spot. Yuanji was hit by an arrow and fled; Yuchi Jingde pursued and killed him.

sentences.zh: 俄而東宮、齊府兵三千攻玄武門，閉不得入。

translations.literal: Before long, three thousand troops of the Eastern Palace and the Qi establishment attacked the Xuanwu Gate but could not get it open.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward, three thousand soldiers of the crown prince's Eastern Palace and Yuanji's Qi establishment assaulted the Xuanwu Gate but failed to force it open.

sentences.zh: 接戰久之，矢及殿屋。

translations.literal: They joined battle for a long time; arrows reached the hall roofs.
translations.idiomatic: The fighting lasted a long while, and arrows struck the palace halls.

sentences.zh: 王左右數百騎至，合擊之，眾遂潰。

translations.literal: Several hundred horsemen of the prince's retinue arrived, struck together, and the host then scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Several hundred horsemen from the prince's guard arrived, attacked together, and the force broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 帝謂裴寂等曰：「事今奈何？」

translations.literal: The emperor said to Pei Ji and the others: 'What is to be done about the affair now?'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to Pei Ji and the others, "What is to be done now?"

sentences.zh: 蕭瑀、陳叔達曰：「臣聞內外無限，父子不親，失而弗斷，反蒙其亂。

translations.literal: Xiao Yu and Chen Shuda said: 'Your servants have heard that within and without there must be no indulgence, that father and son should not show partiality; fail to cut off loss in time and you invite disorder instead.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yu and Chen Shuda said, "We have heard that there must be no indulgence within or without the palace, and that even between father and son there is no room for favoritism. Fail to act decisively when the moment is lost, and you will suffer disorder in return.

sentences.zh: 建成、元吉自草昧以來，未始與謀，既立，又無功德，疑貳相濟，為蕭墻憂。

translations.literal: Jian and Yuanji from the founding struggle onward never shared in counsels; once established they had no merit; suspicion and division fed each other—a calamity within the palace walls.
translations.idiomatic: Jian and Yuanji never took part in planning from the days of the founding struggle onward. Once established, they performed no meritorious service. Suspicion and division fed each other, threatening calamity within the palace walls.

sentences.zh: 秦王功蓋天下，內外歸心，立為太子，付軍國大務，陛下釋重負矣。」

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin's achievements overshadow the realm; within and without hearts turn to him. Install him as crown prince, entrust military and state affairs to him, and Your Majesty will cast off a heavy burden.'
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qin's achievements overshadow the realm, and hearts within and without turn to him. Install him as crown prince and entrust him with military and state affairs, and Your Majesty will be rid of a heavy burden."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「此吾誌也！」

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'This has long been my wish!'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "That has long been my wish!"

sentences.zh: 乃召秦王至，尉撫之曰：「朕幾有投杼之惑。」

translations.literal: He then summoned the Prince of Qin, comforted him, and said: 'I nearly fell prey to the suspicion of the jade pestle.'
translations.idiomatic: He then summoned the Prince of Qin, comforted him, and said, "I nearly succumbed to groundless suspicion."

sentences.zh: 秦王號泣不能止。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin wailed and could not stop.
translations.idiomatic: The prince wailed and could not stop.

sentences.zh: 建成死年三十八。

translations.literal: Jian died at age thirty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was thirty-eight when he died.

sentences.zh: 長子承宗為太原王，早卒；

translations.literal: His eldest son Chengzong was Prince of Taiyuan and died early.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Chengzong, Prince of Taiyuan, died young.

sentences.zh: 承道安陸王，承德河東王，承訓武安王，承明汝南王，承義巨鹿王，皆坐誅。

translations.literal: Chengdao was Prince of Anlu, Chengde Prince of Hedong, Chengxun Prince of Wu'an, Chengming Prince of Runan, Chengyi Prince of Julu—all were executed on account of the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Chengdao was Prince of Anlu, Chengde Prince of Hedong, Chengxun Prince of Wu'an, Chengming Prince of Runan, and Chengyi Prince of Julu—all were put to death for their connection to the plot.

sentences.zh: 詔除建成、元吉屬籍。

translations.literal: An edict removed Jian and Yuanji from the clan register.
translations.idiomatic: An edict struck Jian and Yuanji from the imperial clan register.

sentences.zh: 其黨疑懼，更相告，廬江王瑗遂反。

translations.literal: Their partisans, fearful and suspicious, denounced one another; the Prince of Lujiang, Yuan, then rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Their followers, fearful and suspicious, denounced one another, and the Prince of Lujiang, Yuan, rose in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 乃下詔建成、元吉、瑗支黨不得相告訐，由是遂安。

translations.literal: An edict was then issued that factions of Jian, Yuanji, and Yuan must not inform or impeach one another; thereby the realm was settled.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was then issued forbidding the factions of Jian, Yuanji, and Yuan to inform or impeach one another, and the realm was calmed.

sentences.zh: 太宗立，追封建成為息王，謚曰隱，以禮改葬，詔東宮舊臣皆會，帝於宜秋門哭之，以子福為後。

translations.literal: When Taizong took the throne, he posthumously enfeoffed Jian as Prince of Xi with the posthumous title Hidden, reburied him with full rites, ordered former Eastern Palace officials to assemble, wept for him at the Yichun Gate, and appointed his son Fu as heir.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong came to the throne, he posthumously enfeoffed Jian as Prince of Xi with the posthumous title Hidden, had him reburied with full rites, summoned former Eastern Palace officials to attend, wept for him at the Yichun Gate, and appointed his son Fu as heir.

sentences.zh: 十六年，追今贈。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, further posthumous gifts were conferred.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year of his reign, further posthumous honors were granted.

sentences.zh: 宇文穎者，代人。

translations.literal: Yuwen Ying was a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Ying was a native of Dai.

sentences.zh: 自李密所來降，為農圃監，封化政郡公。

translations.literal: He came over in surrender from Li Mi, was made Supervisor of Agriculture and Gardens, and enfeoffed as Duke of Huazheng commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He surrendered from Li Mi's camp, was appointed Supervisor of Agriculture and Gardens, and enfeoffed as Duke of Huazheng.

sentences.zh: 性貪昏，與元吉厚善，故豫文幹謀。

translations.literal: Greedy and muddled by nature, he was on close terms with Yuanji and therefore took part in Wen'gan's plot.
translations.idiomatic: Greedy and dull-witted by nature, he was on intimate terms with Yuanji and therefore joined Wen'gan's conspiracy.

sentences.zh: 事敗，帝責曰：「朕以文幹叛，故遣卿，乃同逆邪？」

translations.literal: When the affair failed, the emperor reproached him: 'I sent you because Wen'gan had rebelled—yet you joined the rebels?'
translations.idiomatic: When the plot failed, the emperor reproached him, saying, "I sent you because Wen'gan had rebelled—yet you joined the rebels?"

sentences.zh: 穎無以對，斬之。

translations.literal: Ying had no reply and was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Ying had no answer and was beheaded.

sentences.zh: 巢刺王元吉小字三胡。

translations.literal: Nest-Stab Prince Yuanji had the childhood name Sanhu.
translations.idiomatic: Nest-Stab Prince Yuanji had the childhood name Sanhu.

sentences.zh: 高祖兵已西，留守太原，封姑臧郡公，進齊國，總十五郡諸軍事，加鎮北將軍、太原道行軍元帥。

translations.literal: When Gaozu's army had marched west, he remained to hold Taiyuan, was enfeoffed Duke of Guzang commandery, advanced to Prince of Qi, oversaw military affairs across fifteen commanderies, and was made General Who Pacifies the North and campaign marshal on the Taiyuan circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu's army marched west, Yuanji remained to hold Taiyuan. He was enfeoffed as Duke of Guzang, advanced to Prince of Qi, placed in overall charge of military affairs across fifteen commanderies, and made General Who Pacifies the North and campaign marshal on the Taiyuan circuit.

sentences.zh: 帝受禪，進王齊，為并州總管。

translations.literal: When the emperor accepted the abdication, he was advanced to Prince of Qi and made regional commander of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor took the throne, Yuanji was advanced to Prince of Qi and made regional commander of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，元吉生，太穆皇后惡其貌，不舉，侍媼陳善意私乳之。

translations.literal: At first, when Yuanji was born, Empress Dowager Taimu disliked his appearance and would not rear him; the attendant wet nurse Chen Shan'i privately nursed him.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when Yuanji was born, Empress Dowager Taimu disliked his looks and refused to rear him. The attendant wet nurse Chen Shan'i nursed him in secret.

sentences.zh: 及長，猜鷙好兵，居邊久，益驕侈。

translations.literal: When he grew up, he was suspicious, fierce, and fond of arms; long residence on the frontier made him ever more arrogant and extravagant.
translations.idiomatic: As he grew up, he became suspicious, fierce, and fond of war. Long years on the frontier made him ever more arrogant and extravagant.

sentences.zh: 常令奴客、諸妾數百人被甲習戰，相擊刺，死傷甚眾。

translations.literal: He often had hundreds of slaves, retainers, and concubines don armor and drill in combat, striking at one another; casualties were very many.
translations.idiomatic: He often had hundreds of slaves, retainers, and concubines put on armor and drill in combat, striking at one another, with many killed and wounded.

sentences.zh: 後元吉中創，善意止之，元吉恚，命壯士拉死，私謚慈訓夫人。

translations.literal: Later Yuanji suffered a wound; Shan'i stopped the drill; Yuanji was enraged and had brawny men tear her apart; he privately gave her the posthumous title Lady Compassionate Instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yuanji was wounded in the drills. Shan'i tried to stop them, and Yuanji in a rage had strong men tear her apart. He privately gave her the posthumous title Lady Compassionate Instruction.

sentences.zh: 劉武周略汾、晉，詔遣右衛將軍宇文歆助守。

translations.literal: Liu Wuzhou overran Fen and Jin; an edict dispatched Right Guards General Yuwen Xin to assist in the defense.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Wuzhou overran Fen and Jin, an edict dispatched Right Guards General Yuwen Xin to help hold the defense.

sentences.zh: 元吉喜鷹狗，出常載罝罔三十車，曰：「我寧三日不食，不可一日不獵。」

translations.literal: Yuanji loved hawks and hunting dogs; when he went out he routinely loaded thirty carts with nets and snares, saying: 'I would rather go three days without food than one day without the hunt.'
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji loved hawks and hunting dogs. When he went out he routinely took thirty cartloads of nets and snares, saying, "I would rather go three days without eating than one day without hunting."

sentences.zh: 夜潛出淫民家，府門不閉。

translations.literal: At night he stole out to ravish commoners' households; the prefectural gate was left unclosed.
translations.idiomatic: At night he slipped out to assault commoners' households, and the prefectural gates were left unguarded.

sentences.zh: 歆驟諫，不納，乃顯表於帝曰：「王數出與竇誕縱獵，蹂民田，縱左右攘奪，畜產為盡。

translations.literal: Xin urgently remonstrated but was not heeded; he then submitted an open memorial to the emperor: 'The prince repeatedly goes out with Dou Dan to hunt recklessly, tramples the people's fields, lets his followers seize and plunder, and devours their livestock to exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: Xin remonstrated urgently but was not heeded. He then submitted an open memorial to the emperor, saying, "The prince repeatedly goes out with Dou Dan to hunt without restraint, tramples the people's fields, lets his followers seize and plunder, and leaves their livestock utterly depleted.

sentences.zh: 每射於道，觀人避矢以為樂。

translations.literal: Each time he shoots along the road, he takes delight in watching people dodge his arrows.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he shot along the road, he took pleasure in watching people dodge his arrows.

sentences.zh: 百姓怨毒。

translations.literal: The common people are full of resentment and poison.
translations.idiomatic: The common people were seething with resentment.

sentences.zh: 不可與共守。」

translations.literal: He cannot be trusted to hold the defense.'
translations.idiomatic: He cannot be entrusted with the defense."

sentences.zh: 有詔召還。

translations.literal: An edict was issued to recall him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was issued recalling him.

sentences.zh: 元吉密諷民詣闕請，乃得歸。

translations.literal: Yuanji secretly prompted the people to go to the palace and petition; only then was he allowed to return.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji secretly urged the people to go to court and petition on his behalf, and only then was he allowed to return.

sentences.zh: 武周以五千騎屯黃蛇嶺，元吉使將軍張達以步卒百人嘗寇，達辭兵少，強之，至則盡沒。

translations.literal: Wuzhou encamped five thousand cavalry at Huangshe Ridge; Yuanji sent General Zhang Da with a hundred infantry to probe the enemy; Da said the force was too small but was compelled; on arrival they were wiped out.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhou encamped five thousand cavalry at Huangshe Ridge. Yuanji sent General Zhang Da with a hundred foot soldiers to probe the enemy. Da protested that the force was too small but was overruled; on arrival they were annihilated.

sentences.zh: 達怒，導武周陷榆次。

translations.literal: Da in anger guided Wuzhou to take Yuci.
translations.idiomatic: Da in anger guided Wuzhou to capture Yuci.

sentences.zh: 元吉保祁，賊急攻之，遁還并州，賊張甚。

translations.literal: Yuanji held Qi county; the bandits pressed the attack hard; he fled back to Bingzhou; the rebels flourished greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji held Qi, but the rebels pressed the attack hard. He fled back to Bingzhou while the enemy grew ever stronger.

sentences.zh: 元吉紿司馬劉德威曰：「公以老弱守，吾率銳士拒賊。」

translations.literal: Yuanji deceived Chief Administrator Liu Dewei, saying: 'You hold the defense with the old and weak; I shall lead crack troops to repel the bandits.'
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji deceived Chief Administrator Liu Dewei, saying, "You hold the defense with the old and weak troops; I shall lead crack soldiers to repel the rebels."

sentences.zh: 因賫寶物、攜妻妾夜出，委軍奔京師，并州陷。

translations.literal: He then packed valuables, took his wives and concubines out by night, abandoned the army, and fled to the capital; Bingzhou fell.
translations.idiomatic: He then loaded up valuables, took his wives and concubines out by night, abandoned the army, and fled to the capital. Bingzhou fell.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，自是嘗令從秦王征討，不復顓軍矣。

translations.literal: The emperor was furious; thereafter he was often ordered to follow the Prince of Qin on campaigns and was no longer entrusted with independent command.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious. From then on Yuanji was usually ordered to follow the Prince of Qin on campaigns and was no longer given independent command of an army.

sentences.zh: 尋授侍中、襄州道行臺尚書令、稷州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Palace Attendant, chief minister of the Xiangzhou circuit staff, and governor of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed Palace Attendant, chief minister of the Xiangzhou circuit staff, and governor of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 秦王圍東都，竇建德來援，王以精騎逆戰，留元吉、屈突通守，而世充易之，輒出兵，元吉設伏劫之，斬首八百級，禽其將。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Qin besieged the Eastern Capital, Dou Jiande came to relieve it; the prince engaged him with elite cavalry; Yuanji and Yuchi Tong were left to guard; Shichong took them lightly and sallied forth repeatedly; Yuanji set an ambush, raided them, took eight hundred heads, and captured their generals.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Qin besieged the Eastern Capital, Dou Jiande came to relieve it. The prince engaged him with elite cavalry while Yuanji and Yuchi Tong were left to hold the line. Wang Shichong took them lightly and sallied forth again and again. Yuanji set an ambush, raided them, took eight hundred heads, and captured enemy generals.

sentences.zh: 東都平，拜司空，賜袞冕服、鼓吹二部、班劍二十人、黃金二千斤，與太子、秦王得三爐鑄錢。

translations.literal: When the Eastern Capital was pacified, he was appointed Grand Preceptor, granted robes with twelve insignia, two ensembles of ceremonial musicians, twenty protocol swords, two thousand jin of gold; with the crown prince and Prince of Qin he was given rights to three mints for coinage.
translations.idiomatic: When the Eastern Capital was pacified, he was appointed Minister of Works and granted robes of the highest rank, two ensembles of ceremonial musicians, twenty protocol swords, and two thousand jin of gold. Together with the crown prince and the Prince of Qin, he was granted the right to operate three mints.

sentences.zh: 累進司徒，兼侍中、并州大都督。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Minister of Works, and concurrently Palace Attendant and great regional commander of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to Minister of Works and concurrently served as Palace Attendant and great regional commander of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 時秦王有功，而太子不為中外所屬，元吉喜亂，欲並圖之。

translations.literal: At that time the Prince of Qin had merit, while the crown prince lacked support within and without; Yuanji delighted in turmoil and wished to destroy them both.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Prince of Qin had won great merit, while the crown prince lacked support within and without the court. Yuanji delighted in turmoil and wished to destroy them both.

sentences.zh: 乃構於太子曰：「秦王功業日隆，為上所愛，殿下雖為太子，位不安，不早計，還踵受禍矣，請為殿下殺之。」

translations.literal: He therefore slandered the crown prince, saying: 'The Prince of Qin's achievements grow daily and the emperor loves him; though you are crown prince, your position is not secure—if you do not plan early, you will soon suffer calamity in his wake. Please let me kill him for you, Your Highness.'
translations.idiomatic: He therefore turned the crown prince against his rival, saying, "The Prince of Qin's achievements grow daily, and the emperor favors him. Though you are crown prince, your position is not secure. If you do not act soon, calamity will follow hard upon you. Let me kill him for you, Your Highness."

sentences.zh: 太子不忍，元吉數諷不已，許之。

translations.literal: The crown prince could not bear it; Yuanji repeatedly pressed him until he agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince could not bring himself to agree, but Yuanji pressed him again and again until he consented.

sentences.zh: 於是邀結宮掖，厚賂中書令封德彜，使為遊說，帝遂疏秦王，愛太子。

translations.literal: They then recruited the inner palace, lavishly bribed Secretariat Director Feng Deyi to lobby on their behalf; the emperor grew distant from the Prince of Qin and favored the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: They then cultivated ties in the inner palace and lavishly bribed Secretariat Director Feng Deyi to lobby on their behalf. The emperor grew distant from the Prince of Qin and favored the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 元吉乃多匿亡命壯士，厚賜之，使為用。

translations.literal: Yuanji then hid many fleeing bravos and rewarded them richly to serve him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji then harbored many fugitive bravos, rewarded them lavishly, and put them to use.

sentences.zh: 元吉記室參軍榮九思為詩刺之曰：「丹青飾成慶，玉帛禮專諸。」

translations.literal: Yuanji's registrar-attendant Rong Jiusi wrote a poem to satirize him: 'With paint one adorns Cheng Qing; with silk and jade one honors Zhuan Zhu.'
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji's registrar-attendant Rong Jiusi wrote a satirical poem: "With paint one adorns Cheng Qing; with silk and jade one honors Zhuan Zhu."

sentences.zh: 元吉見之，弗悟也。

translations.literal: When Yuanji saw it, he did not understand.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanji read it, he did not understand the allusion.

sentences.zh: 其典簽裴宣儼免官，往事秦府，元吉疑事泄，鴆殺之。

translations.literal: His chief clerk Pei Xuanyi was dismissed and went to the Qin prince's establishment; Yuanji suspected the plot had leaked and poisoned him to death.
translations.idiomatic: His chief clerk Pei Xuanyi was dismissed from office and went to serve at the Qin prince's establishment. Yuanji suspected the plot had leaked and poisoned him to death.

sentences.zh: 自是人莫敢言。

translations.literal: From then on no one dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: From then on no one dared speak out.

sentences.zh: 秦王嘗從帝幸元吉第，伏護軍宇文寶寢內，將以刺王，太子固止之，元吉慍曰：「為兄計，於我何害？」

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin once followed the emperor on a visit to Yuanji's residence; Yuanji had hid the guard officer Yuwen Bao in his bedchamber intending to stab the prince; the crown prince firmly stopped him; Yuanji said in anger: 'I am scheming for my elder brother—what harm is it to me?'
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qin once accompanied the emperor on a visit to Yuanji's residence. Yuanji had hidden the guard officer Yuwen Bao in his bedchamber intending to stab the prince. The crown prince firmly stopped him. Yuanji said angrily, "I am scheming for my elder brother—what harm is it to me?"

sentences.zh: 突厥郁射設入圍烏城，建成薦元吉北討，乃多引秦王府驍將秦叔寶、尉遲敬德、程知節、段誌玄與行，又籍秦府精兵益麾下。

translations.literal: When the Turks' Yushishe invested Wucheng, Jian recommended Yuanji for a northern campaign; he brought many crack generals from the Qin prince's household—Qin Shubao, Yuchi Jingde, Cheng Zhijie, Duan Zhixuan—and on campaign requisitioned the Qin establishment's elite troops for his own command.
translations.idiomatic: When the Turk leader Yushishe invested Wucheng, Jian recommended Yuanji for a northern campaign. Yuanji brought many crack generals from the Qin prince's household—Qin Shubao, Yuchi Jingde, Cheng Zhijie, and Duan Zhixuan—and on campaign requisitioned the Qin establishment's elite troops for his own command.

sentences.zh: 帝知之，不能禁。

translations.literal: The emperor knew of it but could not forbid it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor knew of it but could not stop him.

sentences.zh: 元吉承間密請害秦王，帝曰：「是有定四海功，殺之無名。」

translations.literal: Yuanji seized an opportune moment to request secretly that the emperor kill the Prince of Qin; the emperor said: 'He has the merit of settling the four seas—killing him would have no justification.'
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji seized an opportune moment to ask the emperor in secret to kill the Prince of Qin. The emperor said, "He has the merit of settling the realm. To kill him would have no justification."

sentences.zh: 元吉曰：「王昔平東都，顧望不即西，散金帛樹私惠，豈非反邪？」

translations.literal: Yuanji said: 'When the prince pacified the Eastern Capital, he lingered and did not proceed west at once, scattering gold and silk to win private favor—is that not rebellion?'
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji said, "When the prince pacified the Eastern Capital, he lingered and did not march west at once, scattering gold and silk to win private favor—is that not rebellion?"

sentences.zh: 帝不應。

translations.literal: The emperor did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not reply.

sentences.zh: 太子與元吉謀：「兵行，吾與秦王至昆明池，伏壯士拉之，以暴卒聞，上無不信。

translations.literal: The crown prince and Yuanji plotted: 'When the army marches, I and the Prince of Qin will go together to the Kunming Pool; brawny men will seize and strangle him; it will be announced as sudden death—the emperor will not disbelieve it.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince and Yuanji plotted together: "When the army marches, I and the Prince of Qin will go together to the Kunming Pool. Brawny men will seize and strangle him. It will be announced as sudden death—the emperor will not disbelieve it.

sentences.zh: 然後說帝付吾國，吾以爾為皇太弟，而盡擊殺叔寶等。」

translations.literal: Then persuade the emperor to give me the realm; I make you crown prince younger brother; and kill Shubao and the rest utterly.'
translations.idiomatic: Then I will persuade the emperor to give me the realm, make you heir apparent to the younger brother, and kill Shubao and the rest to the last man."

sentences.zh: 率更令王晊密以謀告秦王，王召僚屬謀，皆曰：「元吉戾很，使得誌，且不能事其兄。

translations.literal: Court of the Yuchi Wang Zhi secretly reported the plot to the Prince of Qin; the prince summoned his staff to counsel; all said: 'Yuanji is brutal and obstinate; if he gains his wish, he will not even serve his elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Court of the Yuchi Wang Zhi secretly reported the plot to the Prince of Qin. The prince summoned his staff to counsel. All said, "Yuanji is brutal and obstinate. If he gains his wish, he will not even serve his elder brother.

sentences.zh: 往者護軍薛寶以元吉字合之，其文成『唐』，元吉喜曰：『但除秦王，取東宮如反掌耳！』

translations.literal: Formerly Guard Officer Xue Bao combined the characters of Yuanji's name and the writing formed 'Tang'; Yuanji rejoiced and said: 'Only remove the Prince of Qin—taking the Eastern Palace is like turning one's palm!'
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Guard Officer Xue Bao combined the characters of Yuanji's name, and the writing formed the character for Tang. Yuanji rejoiced and said, "Only remove the Prince of Qin—taking the Eastern Palace is like turning one's palm!"

sentences.zh: 為亂未克，已復傾奪，大王不蚤正之，社稷非復唐有。」

translations.literal: Having failed to make trouble, he would already wrest it away; if the great king does not correct this early, the altars will no longer belong to Tang.'
translations.idiomatic: Having failed to make trouble once, he would already try to seize power again. If you, great prince, do not correct this early, the altars of state will no longer belong to Tang."

sentences.zh: 秦王由是定計。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin thereby fixed his plan.
translations.idiomatic: The prince thereby fixed his plan.

sentences.zh: 死年二十四。

translations.literal: He died at age twenty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He was twenty-four when he died.

sentences.zh: 子承業為梁郡王，承鸞漁陽王，承獎普安王，承裕江夏王，承度義陽王，並伏誅。

translations.literal: His sons Chengye was Prince of Liang commandery, Chengluan Prince of Yuyang, Chengjang Prince of Pu'an, Chengyu Prince of Jiangxia, Chengdu Prince of Yiyang—all were executed.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Chengye was Prince of Liang, Chengluan Prince of Yuyang, Chengjang Prince of Pu'an, Chengyu Prince of Jiangxia, and Chengdu Prince of Yiyang—all were executed.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，改葬，追爵海陵郡王及謚。

translations.literal: Early in the Zhenguan reign, he was reburied and posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Hailing commandery with a posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenguan reign he was reburied and posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Hailing with a posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 後改封巢，以曹王明嗣。

translations.literal: Later the fief was changed to Nest; Prince of Cao Ming was made his heir.
translations.idiomatic: Later the fief was changed to Nest, and Prince of Cao Ming was appointed his heir.

sentences.zh: 母萬貴妃，性恭順，為帝所禮，宮中事一一咨決。

translations.literal: His mother was Consort Wan, of gentle and obedient character, honored by the emperor; every matter of the inner palace was referred to her for decision.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was Consort Wan, gentle and obedient by nature and honored by the emperor. Every matter of the inner palace was referred to her for decision.

sentences.zh: 三年，以太宗子寬為嗣，又贈涼州總管、司徒。

translations.literal: In the third year, Taizong's son Kuan was made heir; he was also posthumously given regional command of Liangzhou and the rank of Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, Taizong's son Kuan was made heir, and Yuanji was posthumously given the posts of regional commander of Liangzhou and Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 寬早薨，國除。

translations.literal: Kuan died early and the fief was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Kuan died young and the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 貞觀二年，復以濟南公世都子靈龜嗣，歷魏州刺史，為政威嚴，盜賊不發；

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenguan, Shidu's son Linggui of the Duke of Jinan was again made heir; he served as governor of Wei prefecture, governing with stern authority so bandits did not stir.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhenguan, Linggui, son of Duke of Jinan Shidu, was again made heir. He served as governor of Wei, governing with stern authority so that bandits did not stir.

sentences.zh: 鑿永濟渠，通新市，百姓利之。

translations.literal: He cut the Yongji Canal to reach the new market—the people benefited.
translations.idiomatic: He cut the Yongji Canal to reach the new market, to the people's benefit.

sentences.zh: 薨，子福嗣，降為公。

translations.literal: On his death his son Fusi succeeded; the title was reduced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: On his death his son Fusi succeeded, and the title was reduced to duke.

sentences.zh: 卒，子承況嗣，神龍中為右羽林將軍，同節湣太子死於難。

translations.literal: On his death his son Chengguang succeeded; in the Shenlong era he was Right Guards General of the Feathered Forest and died in the calamity with Crown Prince Minjie of the Same Festival.
translations.idiomatic: On his death his son Chengguang succeeded. In the Shenlong era he served as Right General of the Feathered Forest and died in the upheaval together with Crown Prince Minjie of the Same Festival.

sentences.zh: 荊王元景，武德三年始王趙，與魯、酆二王同封。

translations.literal: Prince Jing Yuanjing—in the third year of Wude was first enfeoffed Prince of Zhao, together with the Princes of Lu and Feng.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jing Yuanjing was first enfeoffed as Prince of Zhao in the third year of Wude, together with the Princes of Lu and Feng.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，累遷雍州牧。

translations.literal: Early in Zhenguan he was repeatedly promoted to governor of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenguan reign he was repeatedly promoted to governor of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 十年，徙封荊。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was transferred to the fief of Jing.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year his fief was changed to Jing.

sentences.zh: 明年，詔荊州都督荊王元景、梁州都督漢王元昌、徐州都督徐王元禮、潞州都督韓王元嘉、遂州都督彭王元則、鄭州刺史鄭王元懿、絳州刺史霍王元軌、虢州刺史虢王鳳、豫州刺史道王元慶、鄧州刺史鄧王元裕、壽州刺史舒王元名、幽州都督燕王靈夔、蘇州刺史許王元祥、安州都督吳王恪、相州都督魏王泰、齊州都督齊王祐、益州都督蜀王愔、襄州刺史蔣王惲、揚州都督越王貞、并州都督晉王治、秦州都督紀王慎所任刺史並功臣令世世襲。

translations.literal: The next year an edict named the regional commanders and governors appointed for Jing Prince Yuanjing, Han Prince Yuanchang, Xu Prince Yuanli, Han Prince Yuanjia, Peng Prince Yuanze, Zheng Prince Yuanyi, Huo Prince Yuangui, Guo Prince Feng, Dao Prince Yuanqing, Deng Prince Yuanyu, Shu Prince Yuanming, Yan Prince Lingkui, Xu Prince Yuanxiang, Wu Prince Ke, Wei Prince Tai, Qi Prince You, Shu Prince Yin, Jiang Prince Yun, Yue Prince Zhen, Jin Prince Zhi, and Ji Prince Shen—their posts as governors and the posts of meritorious officials to be hereditary for generations.
translations.idiomatic: The next year an edict named the regional commanders and governors then in office—Jing Prince Yuanjing at Jingzhou, Han Prince Yuanchang at Liangzhou, Xu Prince Yuanli at Xuzhou, Han Prince Yuanjia at Luzhou, Peng Prince Yuanze at Suizhou, Zheng Prince Yuanyi at Zhengzhou, Huo Prince Yuangui at Jiangzhou, Guo Prince Feng at Guozhou, Dao Prince Yuanqing at Yuzhou, Deng Prince Yuanyu at Dengzhou, Shu Prince Yuanming at Shouzhou, Yan Prince Lingkui at Youzhou, Xu Prince Yuanxiang at Suzhou, Wu Prince Ke at Anzhou, Wei Prince Tai at Xiangzhou, Qi Prince You at Qizhou, Shu Prince Yin at Yizhou, Jiang Prince Yun at Xiangyang, Yue Prince Zhen at Yangzhou, Jin Prince Zhi at Bingzhou, and Ji Prince Shen at Qinzhou—and declared that their governorships, together with those of meritorious officials, should pass hereditarily from generation to generation.

sentences.zh: 會長孫無忌等固讓，遂廢不行。

translations.literal: Zhangsun Wuji and others firmly declined; the plan was abandoned and not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Wuji and others firmly declined, and the plan was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 徙鄠州。

translations.literal: He was moved to E prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to E prefecture.

sentences.zh: 永徽初，進位司徒，賜實封至千五百戶。

translations.literal: Early in Yonghui he was advanced to Minister of Works with a substantive fief of fifteen hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yonghui reign he was advanced to Minister of Works and granted a substantive fief of fifteen hundred households.

sentences.zh: 房遺愛謀反，坐子則與往還系獄。

translations.literal: When Fang Yi'ai plotted rebellion, his son Ze was imprisoned for dealings with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Fang Yi'ai plotted rebellion, Yuanjing's son Ze was imprisoned for his dealings with him.

sentences.zh: 時吳王亦抵罪，高宗謂大臣曰：「朕欲從公丐叔及兄死。」

translations.literal: At that time the Prince of Wu was also charged; Gaozong said to the ministers: 'I wish to beg from you the lives of my uncles and elder brother.'
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Prince of Wu was also charged. Gaozong said to the ministers, "I wish to beg from you the lives of my uncles and elder brother."

sentences.zh: 兵部侍郎崔敦禮曰：「陛下雖申恩，不可詘天下法。」

translations.literal: Vice Minister of War Cui Dunli said: 'Though Your Majesty would show grace, you cannot bend the law of the realm.'
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of War Cui Dunli said, "Though Your Majesty would show mercy, you cannot bend the law of the realm."

sentences.zh: 遂賜死。

translations.literal: They were therefore granted death.
translations.idiomatic: They were therefore granted death.

sentences.zh: 久之，追封沈黎王，以渤海王奉慈子長沙嗣，降為侯。

translations.literal: After a long while he was posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Shenli; the son Changsha of Prince of Bohai Fengci was made heir; the rank was reduced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Shenli. Changsha, son of Prince of Bohai Fengci, was made heir, and the rank was reduced to marquis.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，復王爵，以孫逖嗣。

translations.literal: Early in Shenlong the prince's title was restored; Sun Tuo was made heir.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shenlong era the princely title was restored, and Sun Tuo was made heir.

sentences.zh: 薨，無子，國除。

translations.literal: On his death he had no son and the fief was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: On his death he left no son, and the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 漢王元昌，初王魯，累遷梁州都督，後徙封漢。

translations.literal: Han Prince Yuanchang—first Prince of Lu, repeatedly promoted to regional commander of Liang, later transferred to Han.
translations.idiomatic: Han Prince Yuanchang was first enfeoffed as Prince of Lu, was repeatedly promoted to regional commander of Liang, and later transferred to the fief of Han.

sentences.zh: 有勇力，善騎射。

translations.literal: He had strength and valor, skilled at riding and archery.
translations.idiomatic: He was strong and brave, and skilled at riding and archery.

sentences.zh: 數觸軌憲，太宗手詔誨督，乃怨望，附太子承乾，通饋謝。

translations.literal: Repeatedly he violated regulations; Taizong sent personal edicts to instruct and supervise him; he then harbored resentment, attached himself to Crown Prince Chenghan, and exchanged gifts.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly violated regulations. Taizong sent personal edicts to instruct and admonish him, but he harbored resentment instead, attached himself to Crown Prince Chenghan, and exchanged gifts with him.

sentences.zh: 來朝京師，宿東宮，嘗有醜語；

translations.literal: When he came to court in the capital he lodged in the Eastern Palace and once uttered vile words.
translations.idiomatic: When he came to court in the capital he lodged in the Eastern Palace and once spoke vile words.

sentences.zh: 又見帝側有宮人善琵琶，乃曰：「事成幸賜我。」

translations.literal: He also saw a palace woman at the emperor's side skilled at the pipa and said: 'When the affair succeeds, grant her to me, I pray.
translations.idiomatic: He also saw a palace woman beside the emperor who was skilled at the pipa and said, "When the affair succeeds, grant her to me.

sentences.zh: 承乾許之，割臂血盟。

translations.literal: Chengqian agreed; they cut their arms for a blood oath.
translations.idiomatic: Chengqian agreed, and they cut their arms to seal a blood oath.

sentences.zh: 事敗，帝弗忍誅，欲免死，高士廉、李勣等固爭不奉詔，乃賜死，國除。

translations.literal: When the affair failed, the emperor could not bear to execute him and wished to spare his life; Gao Shilian, Li Ji, and others firmly protested and refused to obey the edict; he was then granted death, and the fief was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot failed, the emperor could not bring himself to execute him and wished to spare his life, but Gao Shilian, Li Ji, and others strenuously objected and would not carry out the order; he was then granted death, and the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 酆悼王元亨，貞觀二年，授金州刺史，之籓，太宗憐其幼，思之，數遣使為勞問，賜金盞以娛樂之。

translations.literal: Feng (posthumous title Mourning) Prince Yuanheng—in the second year of Zhenguan was appointed prefect of Jin, went to his fief; Taizong pitied his youth, missed him, repeatedly sent envoys to console him, and bestowed golden cups for his amusement.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yuanheng of Feng, posthumously styled Mourning, was in the second year of Zhenguan appointed prefect of Jin and sent to his fief. Taizong pitied his youth and missed him, repeatedly dispatching envoys to inquire after him and bestowing golden cups for his diversion.

sentences.zh: 六年薨，無子，國除。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he died; no son; the fief was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he died without a son, and the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 徐康王元禮性恭畏，善騎射。

translations.literal: Xu (posthumous title Kang) Prince Yuanli was by nature respectful and wary, skilled at riding and archery.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yuanli of Xu, posthumously styled Kang, was by nature respectful and cautious, and skilled at riding and archery.

sentences.zh: 始王鄭，即授鄭州刺史。

translations.literal: First enfeoffed as Prince of Zheng, and at once made prefect of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was first enfeoffed as Prince of Zheng and at once appointed prefect of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 後徙王徐，遷徐州都督。

translations.literal: Later transferred to Prince of Xu, moved to regional commander of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: He was later transferred to Prince of Xu and made regional commander of Xu.

sentences.zh: 為絳州刺史，有治名，璽書勞勉，實封至千戶。

translations.literal: As prefect of Jiang, he had a reputation for good governance; imperial letters praised and encouraged him; actual enfeoffment reached one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect of Jiang he earned a name for good governance; the emperor sent sealed letters of praise and encouragement, and his actual enfeoffment rose to one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 永徽中，加司徒，兼潞州刺史。

translations.literal: During Yonghui, elevated to Minister of State and concurrently prefect of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yonghui era he was promoted to Minister of State and concurrently served as prefect of Lu.

sentences.zh: 薨，贈太尉、冀州大都督，陪葬獻陵。

translations.literal: On his death, posthumously Minister of State, regional commander-in-chief of Ji, buried at Xianling.
translations.idiomatic: On his death he was posthumously made Minister of State and regional commander-in-chief of Ji, and was buried at Xianling.

sentences.zh: 三子，茂為淮南王，餘爵公。

translations.literal: Three sons; Mao was Prince of Huainan, the rest enfeoffed as dukes.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Mao was made Prince of Huainan, and the rest were enfeoffed as dukes.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，以茂子璀嗣，開元中，為宗正員外卿。
