translations.literal: Early in Shenlong, Mao's son Cui succeeded; in Kaiyuan he was acting vice director of the Directorate of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shenlong era Mao's son Cui succeeded to the title; in the Kaiyuan era he served as acting vice director of the Directorate of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 薨，子延年嗣。

translations.literal: On his death, son Yannian succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: On his death his son Yannian succeeded.

sentences.zh: 拔汗那王入朝，延年將以女嫁之，為右相李林甫劾奏，貶文安郡別駕，終餘杭司馬，國除。

translations.literal: When the king of Bakhara came to court, Yannian was about to marry his daughter to him; Grand Counsellor Li Linfu impeached him; he was demoted to vice-prefect of Wen'an, ended as secretary of Yuhang, and the fief was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: When the king of Bakhara came to court, Yannian was about to give his daughter in marriage to him; the Grand Counsellor Li Linfu impeached him; he was demoted to vice-prefect of Wen'an and ended his career as secretary of Yuhang, and the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 永泰初，延年婿黔中觀察使趙國珍言諸朝，詔以其子諷嗣王。

translations.literal: Early in Yongtai, Yannian's son-in-law Zhao Guozhen, observation commissioner of Qianzhong, spoke to the court; an edict made his son Feng heir to the prince.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yongtai era Yannian's son-in-law Zhao Guozhen, observation commissioner of Qianzhong, petitioned the court; an edict made his son Feng heir to the princely title.

sentences.zh: 貞觀九年，更封韓，遷滑州都督。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Zhenguan, further enfeoffed as Han, moved to regional commander of Hua.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Zhenguan he was further enfeoffed as Prince of Han and made regional commander of Hua.

sentences.zh: 高宗末，為澤州刺史。

translations.literal: Late in Gaozong's reign, he was prefect of Ze.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Gaozong's reign he served as prefect of Ze.

sentences.zh: 武後得政，進授太尉，徙定州刺史，以霍王元軌為司徒，舒王元名為司空，滕王元嬰開府儀同三司，魯王靈夔太子太師，越王貞太子太傅，紀王慎太子太保，外示尊寵，而內將圖之。

translations.literal: When Empress Wu seized power, he was promoted to Grand Minister of State and moved to prefect of Ding; Prince of Huo Yuan Gui was made Minister of State, Prince of Shu Yuan Ming Minister of Works, Prince of Teng Yuan Ying Palace Captain of Honor Guards with Rank Equal to the Three Excellencies, Prince of Lu Ling Kui Crown Prince Grand Tutor, Prince of Yue Zhen Crown Prince Grand Mentor, Prince of Ji Shen Crown Prince Grand Guardian—outward show of honor while inwardly plotting against them.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu seized power she promoted him to Grand Minister of State and transferred him to prefect of Ding; she made Prince of Huo Yuan Gui Minister of State, Prince of Shu Yuan Ming Minister of Works, Prince of Teng Yuan Ying Palace Captain of Honor Guards with rank equal to the Three Excellencies, Prince of Lu Ling Kui Crown Prince Grand Tutor, Prince of Yue Zhen Crown Prince Grand Mentor, and Prince of Ji Shen Crown Prince Grand Guardian—an outward show of honor while she plotted against them within.

sentences.zh: 垂拱中，元嘉徙絳州刺史，與子譔及越王子沖糾合宗室同舉兵，未發。

translations.literal: During Chuigong, Yuanjia was moved to prefect of Jiang; with his son Zuan and the Prince of Yue's son Chong he gathered the imperial clansmen to rise together, but had not yet acted.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chuigong era Yuanjia was transferred to prefect of Jiang; with his son Zuan and the Prince of Yue's son Chong he rallied the imperial clansmen to raise troops together, but had not yet moved.

sentences.zh: 會武後詔宗室朝明堂，元嘉遣使告諸王曰：「大享後，太后必盡誅諸王，不如先事起。

translations.literal: When Empress Wu summoned the imperial clan to the Bright Hall, Yuanjia sent messengers to tell the princes: 'After the great sacrifice, the Empress Dowager will surely execute all the princes; better to act first.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu summoned the imperial clan to the Bright Hall, Yuanjia sent messengers to tell the princes, "After the great sacrifice the Empress Dowager will surely execute all the princes; we had better rise first.

sentences.zh: 不然，李氏無種矣。」

translations.literal: Otherwise the house of Li will have no descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise the house of Li will be extinguished.

sentences.zh: 乃為中宗詔，督諸王發兵。

translations.literal: He then forged an edict in Zhongzong's name, directing the princes to raise troops.
translations.idiomatic: He then forged an edict in Zhongzong's name ordering the princes to raise troops.

sentences.zh: 沖即以兵五千攻濟州，而諸王倉卒兵不至，遂敗。

translations.literal: Chong at once led five thousand troops to attack Jizhou, but the other princes' forces in haste did not arrive, and they were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Chong at once led five thousand men to attack Jizhou, but the other princes' troops, mustered in haste, did not arrive in time, and they were defeated.

sentences.zh: 元嘉至京師，謀泄，後逼令自殺，年七十。

translations.literal: Yuanjia reached the capital; the plot leaked; the Empress forced him to kill himself at age seventy.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjia reached the capital; the plot was exposed; the Empress forced him to take his own life at the age of seventy.

sentences.zh: 詔改氏元嘉、魯王、越王為「虺」。

translations.literal: An edict changed the clan names of Yuanjia, Prince of Lu, and Prince of Yue to 'Hui' (a poisonous snake).
translations.idiomatic: An edict changed the clan names of Yuanjia, the Prince of Lu, and the Prince of Yue to "Hui"—the name of a venomous serpent, meant as insult.

sentences.zh: 元嘉六子。

translations.literal: Yuanjia had six sons.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjia had six sons.

sentences.zh: 訓，潁川王，蚤卒。

translations.literal: Xun, Prince of Yingchuan, died young.
translations.idiomatic: Xun, Prince of Yingchuan, died young.

sentences.zh: 誼，武陵王。

translations.literal: Yi, Prince of Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was Prince of Wuling.

sentences.zh: 諶，上黨公。

translations.literal: Chen, Duke of Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: Chen was Duke of Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 譔，黃公，工為辭章，孟利貞嘗稱其文曰：「劉鄰之、周思茂不過也。」

translations.literal: Zuan, Duke of Huang, skilled at literary composition; Meng Liyan once praised his writing: 'He surpasses Liu Linzhi and Zhou Simao.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan, Duke of Huang, was skilled at literary composition; Meng Liyan once praised his writing, saying, "He surpasses even Liu Linzhi and Zhou Simao.

sentences.zh: 出為通州刺史，辭疾歸，且謀慮越王也。

translations.literal: He went out as prefect of Tong, pleaded illness and returned, and plotted on behalf of the Prince of Yue.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as prefect of Tong, pleaded illness and returned home, and plotted on behalf of the Prince of Yue.

sentences.zh: 諶通音律，歷杭州別駕，與譔俱死。

translations.literal: Chen understood musical pitch; served as vice-prefect of Hangzhou; died with Zuan.
translations.idiomatic: Chen understood musical pitch, served as vice-prefect of Hangzhou, and died together with Zuan.

sentences.zh: 時籍沒者眾，惟沖、譔家書為多，皆文句詳正，秘府所不及。

translations.literal: At the time many had property confiscated; only Chong's and Zuan's family books were numerous, all with meticulous and correct phrasing, beyond what the imperial archive held.
translations.idiomatic: At that time many had their property confiscated; only Chong's and Zuan's family libraries were extensive, every text meticulous and correct—surpassing even what the imperial archive held.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，追復元嘉爵士，以第五子訥嗣。

translations.literal: Early in Shenlong, Yuanjia's princely rank was posthumously restored; the fifth son Ne succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shenlong era Yuanjia's princely rank was posthumously restored, and his fifth son Ne succeeded.

sentences.zh: 薨，子叔璩嗣，歷國子司業。

translations.literal: On his death, son Shu Guan succeeded, served as vice director of the Directorate of Sons of the State.
translations.idiomatic: On his death his son Shu Guan succeeded and served as vice director of the Directorate of Sons of the State.

sentences.zh: 薨，子煒嗣。

translations.literal: On his death, son Wei succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: On his death his son Wei succeeded.

sentences.zh: 建中中，改王鄆。

translations.literal: During Jianzhong, enfeoffed as Prince of Yun.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jianzhong era he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yun.

sentences.zh: 後懿宗以鄆王即位，復改嗣韓王雲。

translations.literal: Later Emperor Yizong, having ascended from the Prince of Yun, restored the succession to Han Prince Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Later Emperor Yizong, having ascended the throne as Prince of Yun, restored the succession to Han Prince Yun.

sentences.zh: 彭思王元則字彜。

translations.literal: Peng (posthumous title Si) Prince Yuanze, courtesy name Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yuanze of Peng, posthumously styled Si, bore the courtesy name Yi.

sentences.zh: 初王荊，出為婺州刺史。

translations.literal: First Prince of Jing, went out as prefect of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: He was first enfeoffed as Prince of Jing and went out as prefect of Wu.

sentences.zh: 貞觀十年徙王，為遂州都督，以冠服奢僭免。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Zhenguan enfeoffed as Prince of Peng, made regional commander of Sui; dismissed for extravagant crown and robes.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Zhenguan he was enfeoffed as Prince of Peng and made regional commander of Sui, but was dismissed for extravagant headgear and robes.

sentences.zh: 久之，為澧州刺史，更折節厲行。

translations.literal: After a long time, made prefect of Li; then restrained himself and corrected his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was made prefect of Li and thereafter restrained himself and corrected his conduct.

sentences.zh: 薨，贈司徒、荊州大都督，陪葬獻陵。

translations.literal: On his death, posthumously Minister of State, regional commander-in-chief of Jing, buried at Xianling.
translations.idiomatic: On his death he was posthumously made Minister of State and regional commander-in-chief of Jing, and was buried at Xianling.

sentences.zh: 高宗登望春宮，過其喪，哭之慟。

translations.literal: When Gaozong ascended Wangchun Palace and passed his mourning hall, he wept bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong ascended Wangchun Palace and passed his mourning hall, he wept bitterly.

sentences.zh: 無子，以霍王子絢嗣，龍朔中，封南昌王。

translations.literal: No son; Prince of Huo's son Xuan succeeded; in Longshuo, enfeoffed as Prince of Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: He had no son; the Prince of Huo's son Xuan succeeded; in the Longshuo era he was enfeoffed as Prince of Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 薨，子誌暕嗣，開元中，為宗正卿。

translations.literal: On his death, son Zhi Lian succeeded; in Kaiyuan, director of the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: On his death his son Zhi Lian succeeded; in the Kaiyuan era he served as director of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 鄭惠王元懿，始王滕，貞觀中，出為兗州刺史，徙王，厲鄭、潞、絳三州刺史，實封千戶。

translations.literal: Zheng (posthumous title Hui) Prince Yuanyi—first Prince of Teng; in Zhenguan, went out as prefect of Yan; title changed; stern as prefect of Zheng, Lu, and Jiang; actual enfeoffment one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yuanyi of Zheng, posthumously styled Hui, was first Prince of Teng; in the Zhenguan era he went out as prefect of Yan, then his title was changed; he was strict as prefect of Zheng, Lu, and Jiang, with an actual enfeoffment of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 喜經術，數斷大獄，務寬平，高宗嘉之，璽詔褒錫。

translations.literal: He delighted in classical studies, repeatedly adjudicated major cases with leniency in mind; Gaozong applauded this; imperial edicts praised and rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: He delighted in the classics, repeatedly adjudicated major cases with leniency in mind; Gaozong applauded this and issued sealed edicts praising and rewarding him.

sentences.zh: 薨，贈司徒、荊州大都督，陪葬獻陵。

translations.literal: On his death, posthumously Minister of State, regional commander-in-chief of Jing, buried at Xianling.
translations.idiomatic: On his death he was posthumously made Minister of State and regional commander-in-chief of Jing, and was buried at Xianling.

sentences.zh: 霍王元軌，武德六年始王蜀，與豳、漢二王同封，後徙吳。

translations.literal: Huo Prince Yuan Gui—in the sixth year of Wude first enfeoffed as Prince of Shu, together with Princes of Bin and Han; later moved to Prince of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yuan Gui of Huo was in the sixth year of Wude first enfeoffed as Prince of Shu, together with the Princes of Bin and Han, and was later transferred to Prince of Wu.

sentences.zh: 多材藝，高祖愛之。

translations.literal: Multitalented; Gaozu cherished him.
translations.idiomatic: He was multitalented, and Gaozu cherished him.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘗問群臣曰：「朕子弟孰賢？」

translations.literal: Taizong once asked the assembled ministers: 'Among my sons and younger brothers, who is most worthy?
translations.idiomatic: Taizong once asked his assembled ministers, "Among my sons and younger brothers, who is most worthy?

sentences.zh: 魏征曰：「臣愚不盡知其能，唯吳王數與臣言，未嘗不自失。」

translations.literal: Wei Zheng said: 'Your servant is too dull to know all their abilities; only the Prince of Wu has spoken with me many times, and I have never failed to lose my composure.'
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng said, "Your servant is too dull to know all their abilities; only the Prince of Wu has spoken with me many times, and I have never failed to lose my composure in his presence."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕亦器之，然卿以為前代孰比？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'I too esteem him—but whom in former ages would you compare him to?'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I too esteem him—but to whom among former ages would you compare him?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「經學文雅，漢河間、東平也。

translations.literal: He answered: 'In classical learning and refinement, like the Han Princes of Hejian and Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "In classical learning and refinement, like the Han Princes of Hejian and Dongping.

sentences.zh: 至孝行，曾、閔不能過。」

translations.literal: In filial conduct, Zengzi and Min Sun could not surpass him.'
translations.idiomatic: In filial conduct, even Zengzi and Min Sun could not surpass him."

sentences.zh: 帝由是遇益厚。

translations.literal: From this the emperor treated him still more generously.
translations.idiomatic: From this the emperor treated him still more generously.

sentences.zh: 詔納征女為妃。

translations.literal: An edict took Wei's daughter as his consort.
translations.idiomatic: An edict took Wei's daughter as his consort.

sentences.zh: 嘗從獵，遇群豕，帝使射之，筈不虛彀，豕為盡。

translations.literal: Once on a hunt they met a herd of boars; the emperor had him shoot; every arrow found its mark and the boars were all killed.
translations.idiomatic: Once on a hunt they met a herd of boars; the emperor had him shoot; every arrow found its mark, and the boars were all killed.

sentences.zh: 帝撫其背曰：「爾藝過人，顧今無所施。

translations.literal: The emperor stroked his back and said: 'Your skill surpasses others, yet now there is nowhere to apply it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor stroked his back and said, "Your skill surpasses others, yet now there is nowhere to apply it.

sentences.zh: 方天下未定，得若豈不用乎？」

translations.literal: When the realm was not yet settled, had you been there, would you not have been employed?'
translations.idiomatic: When the realm was not yet settled, had you been there, would you not have been put to use?"

sentences.zh: 貞觀七年，為壽州刺史。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Zhenguan, prefect of Shou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Zhenguan he was made prefect of Shou.

sentences.zh: 高祖崩，去官，毀瘠甚，服除，遂菜食布衣終身，至忌日，輒累晝不食。

translations.literal: When Gaozu died he left office; he wasted away severely; after mourning ended he ate only vegetables and wore only plain cloth for life; on anniversaries he would fast for many days without eating.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu died he left office and wasted away severely; after mourning ended he ate only vegetables and wore plain cloth for the rest of his life, and on anniversaries he would fast for many days without eating.

sentences.zh: 十年，徙王，歷絳、徐、定三州刺史，實封至千戶。

translations.literal: In the tenth year enfeoffed as Prince of Huo; served in turn as prefect of Jiang, Xu, and Ding; actual enfeoffment reached one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was enfeoffed as Prince of Huo; he served in turn as prefect of Jiang, Xu, and Ding, with actual enfeoffment reaching one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 所至閉閣讀書，以吏事委長史、司馬。

translations.literal: Wherever he went he shut himself in to read, entrusting administrative matters to his chief administrator and marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he went he shut himself in to read, entrusting administrative matters to his chief administrator and marshal.

sentences.zh: 謙慎未嘗與物忤。

translations.literal: Humble and cautious, he never clashed with others.
translations.idiomatic: Humble and cautious, he never clashed with others.

sentences.zh: 數引見處士劉玄平，為布衣交。

translations.literal: He repeatedly summoned the recluse Liu Xuanping and befriended him as a fellow commoner.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly summoned the recluse Liu Xuanping and befriended him as a fellow commoner.

sentences.zh: 或問王所長於玄平，答曰：「無長。」

translations.literal: Someone asked Xuanping what the prince excelled at; he answered: 'Nothing in particular.
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked Xuanping what the prince excelled at; he answered, "Nothing in particular.

sentences.zh: 問者不解，玄平曰：「人有短，所以見長。

translations.literal: The questioner did not understand; Xuanping said: 'Men have shortcomings, and thus one sees their strengths.
translations.idiomatic: The questioner did not understand; Xuanping said, "Men have shortcomings, and thus one sees their strengths.

sentences.zh: 若王無所不備，吾何以稱之。」

translations.literal: If the prince were complete in every way, how could I praise him?'
translations.idiomatic: If the prince were complete in every way, how could I praise him?"

sentences.zh: 突厥寇定州，元軌令開城門，偃旗幟，虜疑，不敢入，夜遁。

translations.literal: When the Turks raided Dingzhou, Yuan Gui ordered the gates opened and banners lowered; the barbarians were suspicious, dared not enter, and fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: When the Turks raided Dingzhou, Yuan Gui ordered the gates opened and banners lowered; the barbarians were suspicious, dared not enter, and fled by night.

sentences.zh: 州人李嘉運潛結賊，詔窮誅支黨，元軌以寇近且強，人心危，但殺嘉運，餘無所詰，因自劾。

translations.literal: A man of the prefecture, Li Jiayun, secretly joined the bandits; an edict demanded exhaustive punishment of all associates; Yuan Gui said that with the enemy near and strong and hearts uneasy, he executed only Jiayun and questioned no others, then impeached himself.
translations.idiomatic: A man of the prefecture, Li Jiayun, secretly joined the bandits; an edict demanded exhaustive punishment of all associates; Yuan Gui said that with the enemy near and strong and hearts uneasy, he executed only Jiayun and questioned no others, then impeached himself.

sentences.zh: 帝喜曰：「朕固悔之。

translations.literal: The emperor said delightedly: 'I had indeed regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said with delight, "I had indeed regretted it.

sentences.zh: 非王之明，幾失定州矣。」

translations.literal: Were it not for the prince's wisdom, Dingzhou would almost have been lost.'
translations.idiomatic: Were it not for the prince's wisdom, Dingzhou would almost have been lost."

sentences.zh: 王文操者，與賊戰，敗，二子鳳、賢更以身蔽父，得全，二子死。

translations.literal: Wang Wencao fought the bandits and was defeated; his two sons Feng and Xian successively used their bodies to shield their father; he was spared but the two sons died.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wencao fought the bandits and was defeated; his two sons Feng and Xian in turn used their bodies to shield their father; he was spared, but the two sons died.

sentences.zh: 縣抑不為言，元軌廉知之，遣使員祭，上其事。

translations.literal: The county suppressed the report and would not speak of it; Yuan Gui learned of it through investigation, sent an envoy with condolence offerings, and memorialized the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The county suppressed the report and would not speak of it; Yuan Gui learned of it through investigation, sent an envoy to offer condolences, and memorialized the matter.

sentences.zh: 詔贈鳳、賢朝散大夫，旌禮其閭。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously awarded Feng and Xian the title Gentleman for Fraternal Presentation, and honored their neighborhood by ritual display.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously awarded Feng and Xian the title Gentleman for Fraternal Presentation and honored their neighborhood with ritual display.

sentences.zh: 六子，緒為江都王，純安定王，餘皆爵為公。

translations.literal: Six sons; Xu was Prince of Jiangdu, Chun Prince of Anding, the rest all enfeoffed as dukes.
translations.idiomatic: He had six sons: Xu was Prince of Jiangdu, Chun Prince of Anding, and the rest were all enfeoffed as dukes.

sentences.zh: 緒有名譽，為金州刺史，誅。

translations.literal: Xu had a fine reputation; was prefect of Jin; was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Xu had a fine reputation, served as prefect of Jin, and was executed.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，並復官爵，以緒孫暉嗣王，開元中，為左千牛員外將軍。

translations.literal: Early in Shenlong their offices and ranks were all restored; Xu's grandson Hui succeeded to the prince; in Kaiyuan he was captain of the Left Wing Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shenlong era their offices and ranks were all restored; Xu's grandson Hui succeeded to the princely title; in the Kaiyuan era he served as captain of the Left Wing Guard.

sentences.zh: 虢莊王鳳字季成。

translations.literal: Guo (posthumous title Zhuang) Prince Feng, courtesy name Jicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Feng of Guo, posthumously styled Zhuang, bore the courtesy name Jicheng.

sentences.zh: 始王豳，為鄧州刺史。

translations.literal: First Prince of Bin; prefect of Deng.
translations.idiomatic: He was first Prince of Bin and served as prefect of Deng.

sentences.zh: 俄徙王，歷虢、豫、青三州刺史，實封千戶。

translations.literal: Soon moved to Prince of Guo; in turn prefect of Guo, Yu, and Qing; actual enfeoffment one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to Prince of Guo; he served in turn as prefect of Guo, Yu, and Qing, with actual enfeoffment of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 喜畋遊，遇官屬尤嫚。

translations.literal: He delighted in hunting; toward subordinates he was especially insolent.
translations.idiomatic: He delighted in hunting and was especially insolent toward his subordinates.

sentences.zh: 使奴蒙虎皮，怖其參軍陸英俊幾死，因大笑為樂。

translations.literal: He had a slave wear tiger skin and terrify his staff officer Lu Yingjun nearly to death, then laughed for amusement.
translations.idiomatic: He had a slave wear a tiger skin and terrify his staff officer Lu Yingjun nearly to death, then laughed for amusement.

sentences.zh: 薨，贈司徒、揚州大都督，陪葬獻陵。

translations.literal: On his death, posthumously Minister of State, regional commander-in-chief of Yang, buried at Xianling.
translations.idiomatic: On his death he was posthumously made Minister of State and regional commander-in-chief of Yang, and was buried at Xianling.

sentences.zh: 七子，長子翼嗣，為平陽王。

translations.literal: Seven sons; the eldest Yi succeeded; enfeoffed as Prince of Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: He had seven sons; the eldest, Yi, succeeded and was enfeoffed as Prince of Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 薨，子寓嗣。

translations.literal: On his death, son Yu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: On his death his son Yu succeeded.

sentences.zh: 寓無子，爵不傳。

translations.literal: Yu had no son; the title was not passed on.
translations.idiomatic: Yu had no son, and the title was not passed on.

sentences.zh: 次子茂融，以勇聞，垂拱中為申州刺史。

translations.literal: The second son Maorong was known for valor; in Chuigong prefect of Shen.
translations.idiomatic: The second son Maorong was known for valor; in the Chuigong era he served as prefect of Shen.

sentences.zh: 黃公譔與越王謀舉兵，倚以為助。

translations.literal: Huang Duke Zuan and the Prince of Yue plotted to raise troops and relied on him for support.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Duke Zuan and the Prince of Yue plotted to raise troops and relied on him for support.

sentences.zh: 時詔諸王公赴東都，茂融私問所親高子貢，子貢報曰：「來必死。」

translations.literal: When an edict summoned all imperial princes and dukes to the eastern capital, Maorong privately asked his close associate Gao Zigong; Zigong replied: 'If you go you will surely die.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict summoned all imperial princes and dukes to the eastern capital, Maorong privately asked his close associate Gao Zigong; Zigong replied, "If you go you will surely die.

sentences.zh: 乃稱疾不朝，以俟兵期。

translations.literal: He then claimed illness and did not attend court, waiting for the date of the uprising.
translations.idiomatic: He then claimed illness and did not attend court, waiting for the appointed day of the uprising.

sentences.zh: 及得越王書，倉卒不能應，僚屬勸白其書，擢太子右贊善大夫，俄為黨屬所引，誅。

translations.literal: When he received the Prince of Yue's letter he was too hasty to respond; his staff urged him to report the letter; he was promoted to Right Assistant to the Heir Apparent; soon he was implicated as a partisan and executed.
translations.idiomatic: When he received the Prince of Yue's letter he was too hurried to respond; his staff urged him to report the letter; he was promoted to Right Assistant to the Heir Apparent; soon he was implicated as a partisan and executed.

sentences.zh: 巨剛銳果決，略通書史，好屬辭。

translations.literal: Ju was bold, sharp, and resolute; slightly versed in books and histories; fond of composition.
translations.idiomatic: Ju was bold, sharp, and resolute; he had some knowledge of books and histories and was fond of literary composition.

sentences.zh: 天寶五載，出為西河太守。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianbao, went out as prefect of Xihe.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Tianbao he went out as prefect of Xihe.

sentences.zh: 坐資給柳勣支黨，貶義陽司馬。

translations.literal: Punished for funding Liu Ji's faction; demoted to secretary of Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was punished for funding Liu Ji's faction and demoted to secretary of Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 明年，御史中丞楊慎矜得罪，其附離史敬忠與巨善，又坐免官，錮置南賓郡。

translations.literal: The next year Vice Censor-in-Chief Yang Shenjin was punished; his adherent Shi Jingzhong was friendly with Ju and Ju was again dismissed, confined in Nanbin prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Vice Censor-in-Chief Yang Shenjin was punished; his adherent Shi Jingzhong was friendly with Ju, and Ju was again dismissed and confined in Nanbin prefecture.

sentences.zh: 召拜夷陵太守。

translations.literal: Summoned and appointed prefect of Yiling.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned and appointed prefect of Yiling.

sentences.zh: 安祿山陷東京，玄宗方擇將帥，張〓言巨有謀，可屬大事。

translations.literal: When An Lushan took the Eastern Capital, Xuanzong was choosing generals; Zhang Hao said Ju had strategy and could be entrusted with grave affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan took the Eastern Capital, Xuanzong was choosing generals; Zhang Hao said Ju had strategic talent and could be entrusted with grave affairs.

sentences.zh: 召至京師，楊國忠忌之，謂人曰：「小兒詎可使對天子？」

translations.literal: He was summoned to the capital; Yang Guozhong resented him and said to others: "How can a mere boy be allowed to face the Son of Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to the capital. Yang Guozhong resented him and said to others, "How can a mere boy be allowed to face the Son of Heaven?

sentences.zh: 逾月不得見。

translations.literal: More than a month passed without his being granted an audience.
translations.idiomatic: More than a month passed without his being granted an audience.

sentences.zh: 帝知之，召入禁中，對合旨，帝大悅，敕宰相與語，久不得罷，國忠怠，謂巨曰：「比來人多口打賊，君不爾乎？」

translations.literal: The emperor learned of this, summoned him into the inner palace; his replies suited the emperor's intent and the emperor was greatly pleased, ordering the chief ministers to converse with him—they could not dismiss him for a long time; Guozhong grew weary and said to Ju: "Lately many men boast with their mouths of fighting the rebels—are you not one of them?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor learned of this and summoned him into the inner palace. His replies suited the emperor's intent, and the emperor was greatly pleased and ordered the chief ministers to converse with him; they could not dismiss him for a long time. Guozhong grew weary and said to Ju, "Lately many men boast of fighting the rebels with nothing but talk—are you not one of them?

sentences.zh: 巨曰：「誰為相公手打賊者乎？」

translations.literal: Ju said: "Who is the general who has fought the rebels at the chief minister's own hand?"
translations.idiomatic: Ju said, "Which general has fought the rebels at the chief minister's own hand?"

sentences.zh: 乃授陳留、譙郡太守，攝御史大夫、河南節度使。

translations.literal: He was then appointed prefect of Chenliu and Qiao, acting Censor-in-Chief and Henan military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed prefect of Chenliu and Qiao, acting Censor-in-Chief and Henan military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 明日謝，帝驚曰：「何攝為？」

translations.literal: The next day at his audience of thanks the emperor said in surprise: "Why 'acting'?
translations.idiomatic: The next day, at his audience of thanks, the emperor said in surprise, "Why 'acting'?

sentences.zh: 即詔兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: An edict at once made him Censor-in-Chief in full.
translations.idiomatic: An edict at once made him Censor-in-Chief in full.

sentences.zh: 巨奏：「方艱難時，賊多詐，有如陛下召臣，何以取信？」

translations.literal: Ju memorialized: "In these difficult times the rebels employ many ruses; if Your Majesty were to summon your servant as you have, how would one know whom to trust?
translations.idiomatic: Ju memorialized, "In these difficult times the rebels employ many ruses. If Your Majesty were to summon your servant as you have, how would one know whom to trust?

sentences.zh: 乃析契授之。

translations.literal: The emperor then split tally tokens and gave him a portion.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then split tally tokens and gave him a portion.

sentences.zh: 俄兼統嶺南何履光、黔中趙國珍、南陽魯炅三節度使事。

translations.literal: Soon he was also put in overall charge of the three military commissioners He Lüguang of Lingnan, Zhao Guozhen of Qianzhong, and Lu Jiong of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was also put in overall charge of the three military commissioners He Lüguang of Lingnan, Zhao Guozhen of Qianzhong, and Lu Jiong of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 時炅戰數屈，詔貶為果毅，以來瑱代之。

translations.literal: At the time Jiong had repeatedly been defeated in battle; an edict demoted him to guoyi officer and replaced him with Lai Tian.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Jiong had repeatedly been defeated in battle; an edict demoted him to guoyi officer and replaced him with Lai Tian.

sentences.zh: 巨奏：「炅若能存孤城，功足補過，則何以處之？」

translations.literal: Ju memorialized: "If Jiong can hold the isolated city, his merit will suffice to offset his faults—then how is he to be treated?
translations.idiomatic: Ju memorialized, "If Jiong can hold the isolated city, his merit will suffice to offset his faults—then how is he to be treated?

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿隨所處置。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "You may dispose of the matter as you see fit."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You may dispose of the matter as you see fit."

sentences.zh: 巨至內鄉，賊將畢思琛解圍走，遂趣南陽，貶炅白衣從軍，其暮，稱詔復職。

translations.literal: Ju reached Neixiang; the rebel general Bi Sichen lifted the siege and fled; he then hurried to Nanyang, demoted Jiong to commoner status in the army, and that evening proclaimed an edict restoring him to office.
translations.idiomatic: Ju reached Neixiang; the rebel general Bi Sichen lifted the siege and fled. He then hurried to Nanyang, demoted Jiong to commoner status in the army, and that evening proclaimed an edict restoring him to office.

sentences.zh: 京師平，拜留守，兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: When the capital was pacified, he was appointed capital intendant, also serving as Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital was pacified, he was appointed capital intendant, also serving as Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 明年，拜太子少師，兼河南尹、東畿采訪使。

translations.literal: The next year he was made Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, also Henan intendant and Eastern Capital investigation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was made Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, also Henan intendant and Eastern Capital investigation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 征乘牛之出入市者，斥所得佐用度，然稍自盜沒。

translations.literal: He levied those who drove ox-carts into the markets, applying the proceeds to supplement expenses, yet he also embezzled a portion for himself.
translations.idiomatic: He levied those who drove ox-carts into the markets, applying the proceeds to supplement expenses, yet he also embezzled a portion for himself.

sentences.zh: 其妃即張皇后從女弟，內不睦。

translations.literal: His consort was a younger cousin of Empress Zhang; they were not on good terms within the household.
translations.idiomatic: His consort was a younger cousin of Empress Zhang; they were not on good terms within the household.

sentences.zh: 巨選府縣官備使令，妃亦引蒲博少年分黨招貨賄，橈政事。

translations.literal: Ju selected prefectural and county officials to serve as his personal agents; the consort also brought in gambling youths, formed factions, solicited bribes, and distorted government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Ju selected prefectural and county officials to serve as his personal agents; the consort also brought in gambling youths, formed factions, solicited bribes, and distorted government affairs.

sentences.zh: 宗正卿李遵素私張，發巨贓事，貶遂州刺史。

translations.literal: Director of the Imperial Clan Li Zunsu, who favored Zhang, exposed Ju's corruption; he was demoted to prefect of Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Imperial Clan Li Zunsu, who favored Zhang, exposed Ju's corruption; he was demoted to prefect of Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 會段子璋反，道遂州，巨倉卒不知所出，即迎謁，為子璋所殺。

translations.literal: When Duan Zizhang rebelled and passed through Suizhou, Ju in his haste did not know what to do and went out to meet him; Zizhang killed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Duan Zizhang rebelled and passed through Suizhou, Ju in his haste did not know what to do and went out to meet him; Zizhang killed him.

sentences.zh: 子則之，嗜學，年五十餘，尚執經太學，嗣曹王臯薦之。

translations.literal: His son Zezhi loved learning; past fifty he still studied the classics at the Imperial Academy; Prince of Cao Li Gao recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zezhi loved learning; past fifty he still studied the classics at the Imperial Academy; Prince of Cao Li Gao recommended him.

sentences.zh: 貞元二年，繇睦王府長史遷左金吾衛大將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenyuan he moved from chief administrator of the Prince of Mu's establishment to general of the Left Golden Crow Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhenyuan he moved from chief administrator of the Prince of Mu's establishment to general of the Left Golden Crow Guard.

sentences.zh: 坐與從甥竇申善，貶昭州司馬。

translations.literal: Punished for friendship with his cousin Dou Shen; demoted to secretary of Zhaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was punished for friendship with his cousin Dou Shen and demoted to secretary of Zhaozhou.

sentences.zh: 九子，誘為嗣，王臨淮，為澧州刺史，坐贓削爵。

translations.literal: Nine sons; You was heir, enfeoffed as Prince of Linhuai, served as prefect of Li, and lost his title for corruption.
translations.idiomatic: He had nine sons: You was heir, enfeoffed as Prince of Linhuai, served as prefect of Li, and lost his title for corruption.

sentences.zh: 更以次子詢之子微嗣，終宗正卿。

translations.literal: The heir was then changed to Wei, son of the second son Xun, who ended as director of the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: The heir was then changed to Wei, son of the second son Xun, who ended as director of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 子煉嗣，廣德中，亦至宗正卿。

translations.literal: His son Lian succeeded; in the Guangde era he too reached the post of director of the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lian succeeded; in the Guangde era he too reached the post of director of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 鄧康王元裕，貞觀五年始王鄶，十一年徙王。

translations.literal: Prince Yuan Yu of Deng, posthumously styled Kang, was first enfeoffed as Prince of Zheng in the fifth year of Zhenguan; in the eleventh year his title was changed.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yuan Yu of Deng, posthumously styled Kang, was first enfeoffed as Prince of Zheng in the fifth year of Zhenguan; in the eleventh year his title was changed.

sentences.zh: 始王及徙，皆與譙、魏、許、密四王同封。

translations.literal: Both at the initial enfeoffment and at the change of title he was enfeoffed together with the four princes of Qiao, Wei, Xu, and Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Both at the initial enfeoffment and at the change of title he was enfeoffed together with the four princes of Qiao, Wei, Xu, and Mi.

sentences.zh: 累實封至千二百戶。

translations.literal: His actual enfeoffment in aggregate reached one thousand two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: His actual enfeoffment in aggregate reached one thousand two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 好學，善談名理，與典簽盧照鄰為布衣交。

translations.literal: He loved learning and was skilled at discussing abstract principles; with recorder Lu Zhaolin he was friends as commoners.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning and was skilled at discussing abstract principles; with recorder Lu Zhaolin he was friends as commoners.

sentences.zh: 五為州刺史，遷兗州都督。

translations.literal: Five times he served as prefect; he was promoted to regional commander of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Five times he served as prefect; he was promoted to regional commander of Yan.

sentences.zh: 薨，贈司徒、益州大都督，陪葬獻陵。

translations.literal: On his death he was posthumously made Minister of State and regional commander-in-chief of Yi, and was buried at Xianling.
translations.idiomatic: On his death he was posthumously made Minister of State and regional commander-in-chief of Yi, and was buried at Xianling.

sentences.zh: 無子，以江王子廣平公炅嗣。

translations.literal: Having no son, Guangping Duke Jiong, son of the Prince of Jiang, succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Having no son, Guangping Duke Jiong, son of the Prince of Jiang, succeeded.

sentences.zh: 薨，子孝先嗣，開元中，為冠軍大將軍。

translations.literal: On his death, son Xiaoxian succeeded; in the Kaiyuan era he was champion general.
translations.idiomatic: On his death his son Xiaoxian succeeded; in the Kaiyuan era he served as champion general.

sentences.zh: 舒王元名，始王譙，後徙王。

translations.literal: Prince Yuan Ming of Shu was first Prince of Qiao, then his title was changed.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yuan Ming of Shu was first Prince of Qiao, then his title was changed.

sentences.zh: 高祖之在大安宮，太宗晨夕使尚宮問起居，元名才十歲，保媼言：「尚宮有品當拜。」

translations.literal: When Gaozu was in the Great Peace Palace, Taizong morning and evening sent palace ladies to inquire after his health; Yuan Ming was only ten; his nurse said: "Palace ladies have rank and ought to be bowed to.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu was in the Great Peace Palace, Taizong morning and evening sent palace ladies to inquire after his health. Yuan Ming was only ten; his nurse said, "Palace ladies have rank and ought to be bowed to.

sentences.zh: 元名曰：「此帝侍婢耳，何拜為？」

translations.literal: Yuan Ming said: "These are the emperor's serving women—why bow to them?"
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Ming said, "These are the emperor's serving women—why bow to them?"

sentences.zh: 太宗壯之，曰：「真吾弟也！」

translations.literal: Taizong was impressed and said: "Truly my brother!"
translations.idiomatic: Taizong was impressed and said, "Truly my brother!"

sentences.zh: 及長，矜嚴疏財，未嘗問家人生業。

translations.literal: When he grew up he was stern and dignified and free with wealth, and never inquired into his household's livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up he was stern and dignified and free with wealth, and never inquired into his household's livelihood.

sentences.zh: 歷五州刺史，實封至千戶。

translations.literal: He served in turn as prefect of five prefectures; his actual enfeoffment reached one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as prefect of five prefectures; his actual enfeoffment reached one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 子豫章王亶，洛江州，有美政。

translations.literal: His son Prince of Yuzhang Dan presided over Jiangzhou and had excellent administration.
translations.idiomatic: His son Prince of Yuzhang Dan presided over Jiangzhou and had excellent administration.

sentences.zh: 高宗以元名善訓子，手詔褒美。

translations.literal: Gaozong, because Yuan Ming was skilled at instructing his son, wrote a personal edict praising him.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong, because Yuan Ming was skilled at instructing his son, wrote a personal edict praising him.

sentences.zh: 又欲授元名大州，辭曰：「臣忝屬籍，豈以州郡為仕進資邪？」

translations.literal: He also wished to appoint Yuan Ming to a large prefecture; Yuan Ming declined, saying: "Your servant is listed in the imperial genealogy—how could I take prefectures and commanderies as capital for advancement?
translations.idiomatic: He also wished to appoint Yuan Ming to a large prefecture; Yuan Ming declined, saying, "Your servant is listed in the imperial genealogy—how could I take prefectures and commanderies as capital for advancement?

sentences.zh: 治石州二十年，數遊山林，有高蹈意。

translations.literal: He governed Shizhou for twenty years, often roamed mountains and forests, and had the intent to withdraw from the world.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Shizhou for twenty years, often roamed mountains and forests, and had the intent to withdraw from the world.

sentences.zh: 垂拱中，徙鄭州，境接東畿，諸王貴戚為刺史者縱家人暴百姓，元名至，一革之，為治廉威。

translations.literal: During Chuigong he was moved to Zhengzhou; the territory bordered the eastern capital; princes and noble kin serving as prefects let their households tyrannize the people—when Yuan Ming arrived he reformed it all at once and governed with integrity and authority.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chuigong era he was moved to Zhengzhou. The territory bordered the eastern capital; princes and noble kin serving as prefects let their households tyrannize the people—when Yuan Ming arrived he reformed it all at once and governed with integrity and authority.

sentences.zh: 進加司空。

translations.literal: He was further promoted to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was further promoted to Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 子詵，為清河王，早夭。

translations.literal: His son Shen was Prince of Qinghe and died young.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shen was Prince of Qinghe and died young.

sentences.zh: 藹為范陽王，知越王必敗，白髮其謀，得不誅。

translations.literal: Ai was Prince of Fanyang; knowing the Prince of Yue would surely fail, he reported the plot in advance and was spared execution.
translations.idiomatic: Ai was Prince of Fanyang; knowing the Prince of Yue would surely fail, he reported the plot in advance and was spared execution.

sentences.zh: 歷右散騎常侍，為酷吏所害。

translations.literal: He served as right attendant at the gate; he was killed by a cruel official.
translations.idiomatic: He served as right attendant at the gate; he was killed by a cruel official.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，悉追復王爵，以藹子道堅嗣。

translations.literal: Early in Shenlong all princely titles were restored; Ai's son Dao Jian succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shenlong era all princely titles were restored; Ai's son Dao Jian succeeded.

sentences.zh: 江安王元祥，始王許，後徙王，四為州刺史，實封至千戶。

translations.literal: Prince Yuan Xiang of Jiang'an was first Prince of Xu, then his title was changed; four times he served as prefect; his actual enfeoffment reached one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yuan Xiang of Jiang'an was first Prince of Xu, then his title was changed; four times he served as prefect; his actual enfeoffment reached one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 性庸遴，所至營財產無厭。

translations.literal: By nature he was dull and sluggish; wherever he went he amassed property without satiety.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was dull and sluggish; wherever he went he amassed property without satiety.

sentences.zh: 時滕、蔣、虢三王皆貪暴，得其府官者惡之不願行，故時語曰：「寧向儋、崖、振、白，不事江、滕、蔣、虢。」

translations.literal: At the time the princes of Teng, Jiang, and Guo were all greedy and violent, as was the Prince of Jiang'an; those who obtained posts in their establishments hated it and were unwilling to go; hence the saying of the age: "Better to go to Dan, Ya, Zhen, and Bai than serve Jiang'an, Teng, Jiang, and Guo.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the princes of Teng, Jiang, and Guo were all greedy and violent, as was Prince Jiang'an; anyone assigned to their households dreaded the posting and tried to avoid it. Hence the saying of the age: "Better to go to Dan, Ya, Zhen, or Bai than serve Jiang'an, Teng, Jiang, or Guo.

sentences.zh: 元祥魁大，帶十圍，食兼數人。

translations.literal: Yuan Xiang was huge in stature, his girdle ten spans around, and ate enough for several men.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xiang was huge in stature, his girdle ten spans around, and ate enough for several men.

sentences.zh: 韓、虢、魏亦鴻偉，然不逮也。

translations.literal: The princes of Han, Guo, and Wei were also imposing, yet they did not match him.
translations.idiomatic: The princes of Han, Guo, and Wei were also imposing, yet they did not match him.

sentences.zh: 薨，贈司徒、并州大都督，陪葬獻陵。

translations.literal: On his death he was posthumously made Minister of State and regional commander-in-chief of Bing, and was buried at Xianling.
translations.idiomatic: On his death he was posthumously made Minister of State and regional commander-in-chief of Bing, and was buried at Xianling.

sentences.zh: 七子，〓為永嘉王，有禽獸行，誅死；

translations.literal: Seven sons; Zhao was Prince of Yongjia, had beastly conduct, and was executed;
translations.idiomatic: He had seven sons; Zhao was Prince of Yongjia, had beastly conduct, and was executed;

sentences.zh: 皎為武陽王，餘皆爵公，武後時，多及誅。

translations.literal: Jiao was Prince of Wuyang; the rest were all enfeoffed as dukes; in Empress Wu's time many were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao was Prince of Wuyang; the rest were all enfeoffed as dukes; in Empress Wu's time many were executed.

sentences.zh: 皎子叢，以幼流死嶺表，葬南安，人號其冢為「天孫墓」。

translations.literal: Jiao's son Cong, exiled young to the Lingnan frontier, died and was buried at Nan'an; people called his tomb the "Heaven's Grandson Tomb."
translations.idiomatic: Jiao's son Cong, exiled young to the Lingnan frontier, died and was buried at Nan'an; people called his tomb the "Heaven's Grandson Tomb."

sentences.zh: 中宗立，以從子欽嗣王，又以皎封絕，更取弟子繼宗嗣，既而以郡王不襲，降澧國公。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong took the throne, his cousin's son Qin succeeded to the princely title; because Jiao's line had ended, a younger brother's son Jizong was next taken as heir; then because commandery princes were not to inherit, he was reduced to Duke of Li.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongzong took the throne, his cousin's son Qin succeeded to the princely title; because Jiao's line had ended, a younger brother's son Jizong was next taken as heir; then because commandery princes were not to inherit, he was reduced to Duke of Li.

sentences.zh: 密貞王元曉，貞觀中為虢州刺史，實封至千戶。

translations.literal: Prince Yuan Xiao of Mi, posthumously styled Zhen, in the Zhenguan era was prefect of Guo; his actual enfeoffment reached one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yuan Xiao of Mi, posthumously styled Zhen, in the Zhenguan era served as prefect of Guo; his actual enfeoffment reached one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 徙澤州。

translations.literal: He was moved to Ze prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to Ze prefecture.

sentences.zh: 薨，贈司徒、揚州都督，陪葬獻陵。

translations.literal: On his death he was posthumously made Minister of State and regional commander-in-chief of Yang, and was buried at Xianling.
translations.idiomatic: On his death he was posthumously made Minister of State and regional commander-in-chief of Yang, and was buried at Xianling.

sentences.zh: 子穎嗣，為南安王。

translations.literal: His son Ying succeeded as Prince of Nan'an.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ying succeeded as Prince of Nan'an.

sentences.zh: 薨，子勖嗣，早薨。

translations.literal: On his death, son Xu succeeded and died young.
translations.idiomatic: On his death his son Xu succeeded and died young.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，以穎弟亮養子曇嗣。

translations.literal: Early in Shenlong, Ying's younger brother Liang's adopted son Tan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shenlong era Ying's younger brother Liang's adopted son Tan succeeded.

sentences.zh: 開元五年，更詔元曉再從孫東莞郡公徹嗣，徙封濮陽郡王，歷宗正卿、金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Kaiyuan an edict further made Yuan Xiao's great-grandson Dongguan Duke Che heir, moved his enfeoffment to Prince of Puyang, and he served in turn as director of the imperial clan and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Kaiyuan an edict further made Yuan Xiao's great-grandson Dongguan Duke Che heir, moved his enfeoffment to Prince of Puyang, and he served in turn as director of the imperial clan and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 滕王元嬰，貞觀十三年始王，實封千戶。

translations.literal: Prince Yuan Ying of Teng was first enfeoffed in the thirteenth year of Zhenguan; his actual enfeoffment was one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yuan Ying of Teng was first enfeoffed in the thirteenth year of Zhenguan; his actual enfeoffment was one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 為金州刺史，驕縱失度。

translations.literal: As prefect of Jin he was arrogant and unrestrained beyond measure.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect of Jin he was arrogant and unrestrained beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 在太宗喪，集官屬燕飲歌舞，狎昵廝養；

translations.literal: During Taizong's mourning he gathered his staff for feasting, singing, and dancing, and was intimate with menials;
translations.idiomatic: During Taizong's mourning he gathered his staff for feasting, singing, and dancing, and was intimate with menials;

sentences.zh: 巡省部內，從民借狗求罝，所過為害；

translations.literal: touring within his jurisdiction he borrowed dogs from the people for hunting with nets, and wherever he passed he caused harm;
translations.idiomatic: touring within his jurisdiction he borrowed dogs from the people for hunting with nets, and wherever he passed he caused harm;

sentences.zh: 以丸彈人，觀其走避則樂；

translations.literal: he shot pellets at people and took pleasure in watching them flee;
translations.idiomatic: he shot pellets at people and took pleasure in watching them flee;

sentences.zh: 城門夜開，不復有節。

translations.literal: the city gates were opened at night and there was no longer any discipline.
translations.idiomatic: the city gates were opened at night and there was no longer any discipline.

sentences.zh: 高宗以書切責曰：「朕以王至親，不忍致於法，今署下上考，冀愧王心。」

translations.literal: Gaozong rebuked him in a letter, saying: "I, because the prince is very close kin, cannot bear to bring him under the law; now I record a top-grade evaluation in your register, hoping to shame the prince's heart."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong rebuked him in a letter, saying, "Because the prince is very close kin, I cannot bear to bring him under the law; now I record a top-grade evaluation in your register, hoping to shame the prince's heart."

sentences.zh: 久之，遷洪州都督。

translations.literal: After a long time he was moved to regional commander of Hong.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time he was moved to regional commander of Hong.

sentences.zh: 官屬妻美者，紿為妃召，逼私之。

translations.literal: When a staff member's wife was beautiful, he would deceive her on the pretext that the consort summoned her and force her.
translations.idiomatic: When a staff member's wife was beautiful, he would deceive her on the pretext that the consort summoned her and force her.

sentences.zh: 嘗為典簽崔簡妻鄭嫚罵，以履抵元嬰面血流，乃免。

translations.literal: Once he was reviled by Zheng Man, wife of recorder Cui Jian, who struck Yuan Ying's face with a shoe until blood flowed, and he then released her.
translations.idiomatic: Once he was reviled by Zheng Man, wife of recorder Cui Jian, who struck Yuan Ying's face with a shoe until blood flowed, and he then released her.

sentences.zh: 元嬰慚，歷旬不視事。

translations.literal: Yuan Ying was ashamed and for ten days did not attend to business.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Ying was ashamed and for ten days did not attend to business.

sentences.zh: 後坐法削戶及親事帳內之半，謫置滁州。

translations.literal: Later, punished by law, half his enfeoffment households and half his personal attendants in the household register were cut; he was demoted and placed at Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later, punished by law, half his enfeoffment households and half his personal attendants in the household register were cut; he was demoted and placed at Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 起授壽州刺史，徙隆州，復不循法。

translations.literal: He was recalled and appointed prefect of Shou, then moved to Long, and again did not follow the law.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled and appointed prefect of Shou, then moved to Long, and again did not follow the law.

sentences.zh: 隸事參軍事裴聿諫正其失，元嬰捽辱之。

translations.literal: Adjutant Pei Yu remonstrated and corrected his faults; Yuan Ying seized and insulted him.
translations.idiomatic: Adjutant Pei Yu remonstrated and corrected his faults; Yuan Ying seized and insulted him.

sentences.zh: 聿入計具奏，帝遷聿六品上階。

translations.literal: Yu entered the capital to report and memorialized in full; the emperor promoted Yu one grade in the sixth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Yu entered the capital to report and memorialized in full; the emperor promoted Yu one grade in the sixth rank.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗賜諸王彩五百，以元嬰及蔣王貪黷，但下書曰：「滕叔、蔣弟不須賜，給麻二車，助為錢緡。」

translations.literal: The emperor once bestowed five hundred lengths of colored silk on the princes; because Yuan Ying and the Prince of Jiang were greedy, he only sent a letter saying: "Uncle Teng and Younger Brother Jiang need not be given any—give them two cartloads of hemp to help make into cash strings.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once bestowed five hundred lengths of colored silk on the princes; because Yuan Ying and the Prince of Jiang were greedy, he only sent a letter saying, "Uncle Teng and Younger Brother Jiang need not be given any—give them two cartloads of hemp to help make into cash strings.

sentences.zh: 二王大慚。

translations.literal: The two princes were deeply ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: The two princes were deeply ashamed.

sentences.zh: 武後時，進拜開府儀同三司、梁州都督。

translations.literal: In Empress Wu's time he was advanced to Palace Captain of Honor Guards with rank equal to the Three Excellencies and regional commander of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: In Empress Wu's time he was advanced to Palace Captain of Honor Guards with rank equal to the Three Excellencies and regional commander of Liang.

sentences.zh: 薨，贈司徒、冀州都督，陪葬獻陵。

translations.literal: On his death he was posthumously made Minister of State and regional commander-in-chief of Ji, and was buried at Xianling.
translations.idiomatic: On his death he was posthumously made Minister of State and regional commander-in-chief of Ji, and was buried at Xianling.
